articleTitle: An accelerated algorithm for ray tracing simulation based on high-performance computation
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ray tracing tool has played an important role in communication channel modeling. However, accurate simulation with complex scenario will greatly challenge the computational capabilities of personal computer. In this paper, a novel accelerated algorithm for traditional ray tracing tool was proposed based on high-Performance distribute computers. The comparison between traditional ray tracing tool and extended ray tracing tool shown that the accelerating performance for later is highly significant. Numerical results of the simulations show that, jointly using ray tracing tool and high performance distribute computers have been illustrated to be high efficient way for high accurate simulation of channel.

articleTitle: Wideband 3D frequency selective rasorber with two absorption bands
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D frequency selective rasorber consisting of 2D periodic array of open-circuited and short-circuited parallel-plate waveguides. The passband is obtained by the lossless open-circuited parallel-plate waveguide, while two absorption bands located at both sides of the passband are produced by the lossy short-circuited parallel-plate waveguide loaded with a chip resistor. A capacitor is inserted in the short-circuited parallel-plate waveguide, creating an additional resonator, which greatly expands the upper absorption bandwidth. The geometrical details of the proposed FSR are depicted, and simulated performances as well as some analysis are given.

articleTitle: The design of array antennas used for Massive MIMO system in the fifth generation mobile communication
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband, low antenna correlation and high gain array antennas need to be designed for demanding of Massive MIMO system in the fifth generation mobile communication (5G). Firstly, a dual-polarized dipole antenna unit was designed using Finite element numerical calculation method. The operating frequency range of the dipole is 3.5–5.2GHz. Then a method of open scalable modular was introduced to design the array antennas based on subarray of 16 antenna unit, which brought the advantages of high integration degree, scalability and between antenna unit was developed. Finally, the performance of large scale array antennas was simulated. The simulation and measure results show that a bandwidth of 39% (VSWR<1.5) can be realized, antenna correlation between unit is 0.42, and the gain of array antennas composed of 64 unit is 26.8 dB in center frequency. This design results conform to system requirement and provide reference for formulating index standard of base station antenna in the fifth generation mobile communication.

articleTitle: Dual-band microstrip antenna fed by coaxial probe
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to meet the requirement of wireless local area network applications and world interoperability for microwave access applications simultaneously, a dual-band microstrip antenna fed by 50Ω coaxial probe is designed by using the slot loading technique and the short-sheet loading technique. The performances of the antenna are simulated and the size of radiation patch is optimized accordingly. Based on the optimized size parameters, the antenna was fabricated and its performance was measured. Both simulated and measured results show the antenna is suitable for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic scattering characteristics of strait composite random rough surface based on improved hybrid SBR/PO method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to simplicity, hybridization of shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) and physical optics (PO) has been widely used for fast scattering analyses. A composite random rough surface model is presented for describing the concave structure of strait environment. Monte Carlo method is used to build strait composite random rough surface, gauss spectral function is used to simulate ground part of strait, and Pierson Moskowitz (PM) spectral function is used to simulate ocean part of strait. Weighted inverse tangent function is presented to smooth adjacent region. The ray-density normalization (RDN) theory is introduced to improve the SBR method. In consideration of the inartificial cavity construction of strait in natural environment, the improved SBR/PO is used to calculate the electromagnetic scattering of the strait composite rough surface. Electromagnetic scattering characteristics of ground, ocean, and strait composite random rough surface are compared. The impacts of open area of strait concave structure on the curves of bistatic scattering coefficient (BSC) of horizontal-to-horizontal (HH) polarization of strait environment are analyzed. The influence of root mean square (RMS) of ground region on BSC of HH polarization is discussed. The numerical results can use for reference in the fields of remote sensing, detection and inversion of electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: A parallel processing algorithm for multipath clutter cancellation in passive radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The multipath clutter cancellation, the most computationally demanding part of signal processing in passive bistatic radar (PBR), is a key challenge in real time processing. However the previous Extensive Cancellation Algorithm (ECA) versions have their limitations in parallel implementation. In this paper an advanced version of ECA is proposed for multipath clutter cancellation in passive radar. Validated by simulation and theoretical analysis, the proposed algorithm can improve the computation efficiency with an excellent cancelling capability, which provides a valuable basis for real time signal processing in PBR.

articleTitle: A wideband segmented line dipole antenna with stable radiation patterns
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband segmented line dipole antenna with stable radiation patterns in E-plane was proposed and simulated. The configuration of the segmented line helps to reduce the phase lag of the following current which flows toward the same direction consequently. According to the simulated results, the designed antenna covers a wide impedance bandwidth of about 1.34 GHz (2.16-3.5 GHz, 47%). Compared to the conventional dipole with the same dimension, the proposed antenna shows a more stable performance in E-plane radiation pattern.

articleTitle: A broadband terahertz antenna using graphene
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Terahertz wave has been widely used in communication fields due to its unique penetrability, high image analyticity and non-ionizing property, in which antenna is highly necessary. However, traditional terahertz antenna based on noble metal has several problems such as severe loss, low bandwidth and bad radiation performance. In this study, an antenna with graphene radiation and feeding structure was designed based on the impedance characteristic of graphene in terahertz frequency, which has efficiently increased the bandwidth and improved the radiation performance of the antenna. Experimental results indicate that the relative bandwidth reaches to 73.2% and the radiation efficiency retains above 95% when radiation structure is made of graphene; and that the relative bandwidth is almost the same with PEC feeding structure (73.2%) and the antenna has omnidirectional radiation, high gain and radiation efficiency in its impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: A novel widebeam planar patch antenna for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel broad beamwidth patch antenna with a dimension of 80mm60mml.6mm is presented in this paper. It consists of a magnetic dipole, a electric dipole and a ground. The measured 10-dB impedance bandwidth is 5.72–5.96GHz (relatively bandwidth of 4.1%). Over the working band, the E-plane 3-dB beamwidth is as large as with respect to the normal direction. The cross polarization suppression level is better than 20 dB. Details of the antenna design and obtained results are presented.

articleTitle: Non-uniform slotted leaky wave antenna array for broad-beam radiation based on substrate integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel broad beamwidth leaky-wave antenna (LWA) array with non-uniform transverse slots etched on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed. A four-way SIW power divider with equal outputs of phase and amplitude is designed to feed four SIW LWAs with different periodic tapered slots. All these LWAs are working on the -1th spatial harmonic radiation mode, and by choosing periods of slots properly, the radiation beams of them can point to different directions, and therefore, results in a broad beamwidth. Meanwhile, for each SIW LWA, by tuning the length of the radiating slots etched on the top wall of SIW according to the Binomial aperture distribution, the beamwidth can be significantly broadened and the sidelobe level can be effectively reduced. The proposed LWA array shows a 3dB beam width up to 56.8° in the backward side.

articleTitle: Multiband terahertz reflective polarizer based on asymmetric L-shaped split-ring-resonators metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, a multiband reflective polarization converter (RPC) based on asymmetric L-shaped split-ring-resonators(ALSRR) metasurface is theoretically presented. The proposed RPC is able to efficiently convert a linearly polarized (LP) wave to its cross-polarized wave at the four resonant frequencies, besides, it can convert the LP wave to a circularly polarized(CP) wave at the other eight resonant frequencies with a high polarization conversion ratio(PCR). Furthermore, specific elucidation of the surface current distributions of the polarizer reveal the underlying physical mechanism of mutual electromagnetic couplings. The proposed novel polarizer takes favorable advantages of more operation frequency bands for both linear and circular polarization conversions, which indicating great potential applications in terahertz detectors, antennas, imaging and communication systems.

articleTitle: Tunable and broadband radar absorber based on PIN diodes controllable FSS
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a dynamically tunable broadband microwave absorber based on active frequency selective surface (AFSS). The unit cell of the AFSS is composed of PIN diode and two reverse anchor patches. When the bias voltage of PIN diode is changed between 0.6 and 0.78 V, the reflection coefficient of the absorber can be less than -10 dB from 7 to 13 GHz, and the absorbing frequency band can be tuned within the specific range. The fabricated AFSS absorber is light, thin enough and achieves a broad tuning bandwidth. It has the potential to be applied in smart radar absorbing materials.

articleTitle: A dual-band reconfigurable FSS composite structure based on MEMS switches
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band Reconfigurable frequency selective surface composite structure based on MEMS Switch is proposed, which includes eight MEMS switches in one period. The use of the FSS element with the rectangular loop shape is benefit for the realization of dual-band reconfiguration. The FSS composite structure consists of the multilayer substrates and foams, which results in the good electrical performance with the broadband, the dual-band reconfiguration, the stable resonant frequency at the different incident angles and polarizations. Experimental results show that at 0° ~45° incident angle range, Inner envelope relative bandwidth reaches 10% (Transmission efficiency >85% and both polarization).

articleTitle: A high gain bidirectional circular polarization array using bow tie antenna elements for applications in long confined space
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel high gain bidirectional circularly polarized array with the same rotation direction on both sides is proposed in this paper. The array consists of 4 bow tie antennas and operates at 900 MHz. The 4 bow tie antennas are arranged into two linearly polarized endfire sub-arrays which are placed orthogonally, the elements of the two sub-arrays are separated by a distance of one quarter of the free space wavelength in axial direction. To feed the array, a strip line on a substrate with a dielectric constant of 6.0 is used, which makes the guided wavelength equal to one half of the free space wavelength. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth (S11 < − 10dB) is about 12.8% (836–950 MHz) and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth (AR < 3dB) is about 50% (700–1170 MHz). The RHCP gain in the main radiation directions is about 7.3 dBic.

articleTitle: Simulation study of high power microwave damage effect on GaAs HEMT
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the damage effect and mechanism of high power microwave (HPM) on AlGaAs/GaAs pseudomorphic high-electron-mobility transistor (pHEMT) from drain electrode. A two-dimensional electro-thermal model of the typical HEMT is established by simulation software ISE-TCAD. Mobility degradation in high electric field and avalanche generate effect are considered, analyze the distributions and variations of the electric field, the current density and the temperature. The simulation results suggest that intrinsic excitation, avalanche breakdown, thermal breakdown all contribute to damage process. Heat accumulation occurs during the negative half cycle and below the gate near the drain side is most susceptible to burn-out.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-polarized Yagi-Uda antenna for the passive radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized Yagi-Uda antenna for the passive radar is proposed. The antenna consists of two orthogonally installed Yagi-Uda antennas, each of them responsible for one polarization direction. The measurement result shows that the cross polarization discrimination between the two ports is more than 20dB. Antenna patterns for both polarization directions are the same due to the symmetric structure. Experiment for target detecting is conducted with the help of this dual-polarized antenna. Signal processing results show that SNR has been improved through the polarized enhancement technology. Thus Yagi-Uda antenna is a good choice to take into consideration when making dual-polarized antenna for passive radar.

articleTitle: Design of high-gain lens antenna based on phase-gradient metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high-gain and low-profile lens antenna is designed using phase-gradient metasurface (PGMS). The PGMS is a planar structure and is composed of many PGMS units. By changing the size of the metal patch on the unit gradually, we can obtain a transmission phase-shifting range of about 360 degrees. Based on the principle of the phase compensation of the optical lens, the PGMS is designed. Since this phase-gradient metasurface can focus an incident plane wave, therefore, we placed an X-band patch antenna at the focal point of the PGMS as a feed source. In this way, the PGMS and the patch antenna constitutes the entire antenna system together. Then this antenna system is studied using computer simulation. Results show that the designed planar PGMS lens is not only very thin but also can effectively reduce the main beam width and thus enhance the gain of the source antennas. The gain reached 18.7 dB and high directivity was achieved.

articleTitle: PIN tuned phase-gradient-metasurface transmitarray for beam steering application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work presents a study of a PIN tuned active phase gradient metasurface to be used for beam-steering application. The unit cell of the active metasurface consists of square-loop slot loaded with PIN diodes. The phase difference between the unit cells of the metasurface is generated by different position of the PIN diodes welded in the unit cell. And the refractive beam angle of the metasurface can be tuned by changing the state of the PIN diodes. The active metasurface is designed at S band and the effectiveness of the design is validated by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A n-order ultra wideband frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high order novel wide band pass frequency selective surface (FSS). which consist of patch array, lattice array and transmission line (medium layer), the simulation result shows that the 1dB fractional bandwidth of the new FSS is about 50%, the 1dB pass band of three order FSS is from 7.79GHz to 12.49GHz, the insert loss is flat enough in the whole pass band, the suppression in out band increase along with the increasing and the suppression in out band increase to 𢀒15dB at 5GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a novel meander line reader antenna for UHF near-field RFID
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel reader antenna based on electromagnetic coupling between three meander open-ended microstrip lines for ultra-high-frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) near-field applications is proposed in this paper. Meander line units are introduced to generate a strong uniform magnetic-field distribution over a large interrogation with no null zones. The antenna can be adapted to appropriate scenarios conveniently in practical application by increasing or decreasing the number of the meander line units. As an example, a 10-units meander line implemented onto a piece of FR4 printed board is designed and prototyped. The results show that the antenna achieved operating bandwidth about 14 MHz, which covered Chinese UHF RFID standard and produced uniform magnetic field distribution over an interrogation zone of 100 mm×750 mm. Both simulated and measured results are shown to illustrate the good performance of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: A novel omnidirectional horizontally polarized antenna for 4G LTE communications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to increasing demands for a large number of users and a large amount of data transmission, a 4G LTE communication system will require its antenna to have omnidirectional radiation patterns and wide frequency bandwidth. To this end, in this paper, a novel omnidirectional horizontally polarized (HP) antenna is presented for the 4G communication systems. The antenna consists of four pairs of flag-shaped radiators, eight pairs of parasitical striplines. With return loss better than 10 dB, it has a relatively wide fractional bandwidth of 55% working from 1.7 to 3.0 GHz and size of 45×45×2.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Dual-layered metalens for polarization-agile orbital angular momentum waves
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic wave with different orbital angular momentums exhibits potentials for new communication mechanism in both microwave and optical regains. In our recent research, we aim to generate orbital angular momentum waves using the idea of metastructures, for example, the metasurfaces operating as lenses. What's more, for the first time, the polarization property is added to design polarization-agile orbital angular momentum wave front, which is achieved using a two-layered metalenses proposed here. Theoretical and numerical analysis are carried out to validate the design. A new phase relation of metalens is synthesized by combining the radical distribution of aberration of lens and the rotated distribution of orbital angular momentum generation.

articleTitle: Impact of probe ring location on test area performance in 3D MIMO OTA setup
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel concept which is called probe ring location and investigates the impact of probe ring location on the test area performance in 3D MIMO OTA setup. Under different test area size and different channel model, the impact of probe ring location on the test area performance has been discussed. Under different test area size, the test area performance is different. But different channel model have similar impact on test area performance. And with the growth of sphere's radius and probe ring angular, the correlation error doesn't have a linear change but goes up and down. Finally we can concluded that when the target channel model is determined, for a fixed test area size, we could find a group of radius of sphere and probe ring angular to achieve the best teat area performance.

articleTitle: Two methods for BCI probe to improve the high frequency performance
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The main factors that influence the performance of the current injection probe is the core and the coil loop. First of all, considering the permeability, the paper analyzes how to choose the suitable core. Then, the methods are proposed to improve the high frequency performance of bulk current injection (BCI) probe. One is to change the way of coil loops which adopt the symmetrical parallel winding method, so that it will reduce the insertion loss of the probe by increasing the amount of change in the magnetic flux density. The other way is through the parallel resistance to reduce the total impedance of the probe in the high-frequency section, thereby to reduce the insertion loss of the probe. The two methods explore new ideas to improve the BCI probe performance and provides experimental support for the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Comparative study on recovery algorithms for solving electromagnetic scattering problems by compressive sensing
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new incident source is formed based on compressive sensing (CS) theory, in which much information from different incident angle is included. By solving the integral equations under this new incident source, one can obtain the measurements of the induced currents without calculating the problems with a finer angle increment. Especially, different recovery algorithms of CS are studied as used to solve electromagnetic problems over a wide incident angle. Numerical simulation results have shown that the efficiency of the new method can be greatly improved, since the total number of measurements required can be reduced drastically by choosing suitable recovery algorithm.

articleTitle: Graphene-based wideband absorbing screen with radar cross section reduction
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Detection radar is a great threat and challenge for military target like aircraft in modern war. In order to effectively reduce the radar cross section (RCS) from the object's surface to achieve the stealth performance, a novel graphene absorber based on partial non-periodic plane is presented in this paper. The absorption rate of the proposed graphene absorbing screen is more than 90% in the range of 45GHz-160.5GHz with the relative bandwidth of 112.4%. Furthermore, the properties of polarization insensitive and the reduction of RCS are validated and confirmed by the full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Ka band band-stop filter based on complementary split ring and SIW resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a band-stop filter in Ka band is proposed, which is based on substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) resonators and complementary split ring resonators(CSRR). The SIW resonators filter is provided with high pass characteristics. We show that near the resonance point, the impedance characteristics is significantly increased by CSRR. Therefore, we can combine the SIW resonators and CSRRs to change the high pass characteristics and significantly improve the rejection level of the stop-band by etching CSRRs on the top layer in the SIW resonators. The simulated insertion loss of the filter is around - 1dB and the return loss is less than -15dB at the frequency range of 26 to 29 GHz and 32.5 to 36 GHz. In addition, the rejection level is above -20dB from 29.5 to 32GHz.

articleTitle: Three-band polarization-independent spoof plasmon polariton coupler
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a three-band polarization-independent phase gradient metasurface, whose super cell is composed of six different H-shaped elements placed on the substrate layer with back metallic sheet, is proposed to realize conversion between incident wave and spoof plasmon polariton. The measured results conform to the simulated results that the phase gradient metasurface can couple the x and y polarized incident waves into spoof plasmon polaritons at 8.8 GHz, 10.6GHz and 12.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Study of dual-spectral electromagnetically induced transparency in bright-dark mode coupling metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The transmission characteristics of a planar metamaterial, composed of two finite metal strips (with different length) and one double split-ring resonator (DSRR) have been numerically and experimentally investigated in this paper. By varying the length of the two strips slightly, this structure can exhibit single-band and dual-band electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT)-like spectral response in microwave region. The coupled oscillator model is employed to theoretically and quantitatively study the EIT profiles. Our work provides a way to obtain multiple EIT-like effects, and it may achieve potential applications in a variety of fields including filters, sensing, and some other microwave devices.

articleTitle: Extraction of equivalent dipole-moment model based on improve mapped matrix
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It's a common inverse problem to research the near-field coupling and far-field radiation from a PCB circuit through using near-field scanning technique which reconstruct a Dipole-Moment Model based on the near-field plane data. Because of the noise consists in the data, it's a useful method to get a model which is not sensitive to interference by the regularization technique. As different condition numbers of the mapped Matrices, the dipole-moment model has diverse deflection. It's important for getting a stable and accurate dipole-moment model by selecting the best condition number.

articleTitle: On the high-speed railway communication at 30 GHz band: Feasibility and channel characteristics
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Simulations for studying novel high-speed railway millimeter-wave radio propagation channels in urban city are presented in this paper by using verified ray-tracing tool. Based on setups of three antenna beam steering strategies at transceiver, the comparisons among these strategies are given by system feasibility and radio channel characteristics. Numerical results of the simulations are shown to illustrate that adaptive antenna beam steering could greatly improve system performances. However, jointly using fixed and adaptive beam steering is recommended as a trade off between technology implementation and channel performance. Moreover, the system effects from different distances between base station and railroad track are investigated. By selecting a reasonable distance, the detailed radio channel characteristics are extracted including delay spread and Doppler spread, which could serve as a guide for future physical layer design.

articleTitle: A novel split ring slot antenna with multiband characteristics based on SIW
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel split ring slot antenna with multiband characteristics is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of a split ring slot and a ring slot on top surface as the radiator. A novel split ring slot antenna is proposed to realize polarized radiation based on the SIW cavity. Three patch-like radiation patterns and one monopolar radiation pattern at four different frequencies are excited by the single fed antenna. In addition, each operating frequency can be individually adjusted by the ring slot. Moreover, simulated results exhibit that the antenna achieves a maximum gain of 9.2dB in operating frequency with reflection coefficient less than -22.7dB. Its performance is obviously better than other designs, the proposed antenna has features of simple structure and multiband characteristics.

articleTitle: A novel polarization measurement method for large transmitting antenna/antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as a platform, a novel polarization measurement method for large transmitting antenna Z/antenna array is proposed. The mathematical model of the measurement is founded on the decomposition theory of the ellipse polarization microwave. To eliminate the polarization distortion, three mutually orthogonal linearly polarized antennas are selected as measuring reference standard. On the basis of solving the position stability and parameter calibration problems of the reference standard antennas, a verification experiment is practically carried out. Measurement results show that this new method is effective and feasible, thus meeting the practical needs in engineering application.

articleTitle: A dual-band polarized diversity microstrip MIMO antenna with high isolation for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact dual-element high port isolation microstrip MIMO antenna is presented with polarization diversity for wireless local area communication application. The MIMO antenna is comprised of two square patch antenna fed by the aperture-coupling of the microstrip T-shaped structure arranged orthogonally. The high isolation between ports of the antenna elements is obtain by arranging the antenna orthogonally, the aperture-coupling mechanism and the additional strips at the opposite edges of the T-shaped structure. The dimension of the designed MIMO antenna has been greatly decreased for the unique main radiator shared by two antenna elements. The radiation pattern is modified by the square slot near the center of the shared radiator. The simulated and measured results display that the designed antenna offers the impedance bandwidth from 2.40 GHz to 2.50 GHz (0.1 GHz) and from 5.74 GHz to 6.0 GHz (0.26 GHz), and the port isolation is better than − 28.93 dB throughout the first operating band and − 16.79 dB throughout the second operating band. The presented compact microstrip MIMO antenna is probe to be implemented in the portable terminals.

articleTitle: A wideband printed slot antenna using shape blending
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a new design and optimization method of wideband printed slot antenna using a shape blending algorithm. The proposed printed antenna consists of a wide rectangular slot and a tuning stub, which is formed by the shape blending result from a pie and a diamond shape. The method is used to design a printed wide slot antenna for applications in WLAN, WiMAX and UWB. The impact of the antenna geometry on the impedance bandwidth has been simulated, investigated and analyzed.

articleTitle: A wideband omnidirectional antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The antenna array with non-symmetric U-strip stubs antennas is proposed for the wideband and omnidirectional radiation. More specifically, single radiation element with four optimized non-symmetric U-strip stubs antennas provides nice bandwidth characteristics. Three same radiation elements with 30 degrees rotated between adjacent ones are configured in vertical direction to compensate for the radiation depression at higher frequencies. As a result, our proposed antenna array is ensured bandwidth while greatly enhancing the omnidirectional radiation in the whole frequency range. For example, this antenna array achieves an impedance bandwidth of 60.9 % (1.6-3.0 GHz) for VSWR <; 2. A well-formed omnidirectional pattern with gain variation less than 1.5 dB and the maximum antenna gain from 4.5 to 7.3 dBi are obtained in the horizontal plane across the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Multipath effects on time reversal OFDM communications between wireless sensors
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Time reversal orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (TR-OFDM) has recently been received significant concerns in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) applications for its reliable, high-speed, and green communications in multipath environments. However, most publically reported studies were typically performed in strongly multipath channels. In more general non-rich multipath environments, the TR-OFDM performance has not been fully exploited. In this paper, we make a comparative analysis of TR-OFDM communications in different multipath environments. We find that TR-OFDM communications exhibit irremovable bit error floors (BEF) in their bit-error-rate (BER) curves if no channel equalization techniques are applied to the TR-OFDM systems. The underlying reason of the bit error floor is clearly revealed for the TR-OFDM wireless systems.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency of wireless body area networks coexistence
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to the energy limitation of sensor nodes, energy efficiency is one of the main concerns in the design of wireless body area networks (WBANs). Power control plays an important role in reducing network interference and resource management in WBANs. The task of power control is to achieve a certain goal by making use of smaller and suitable power transmission, which depends on the application and network distribution, including interference reduction, throughput maximization, QoS guarantee, topology control, and so on. This paper, using stochastic geometry, develop new nearest neighbor distance power control to increase the energy efficiency of WBANs coexistence.

articleTitle: High-gain dual-polarization higher order mode substrate integrated cavity antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarization higher order mode substrate integrated cavity (SIC) antenna array operating in Ka band is proposed. Cross-shaped radiating slots are employed to achieve the dual polarization performance. An 8×8-elements array is designed by using three layers of double-side printed circuit broads (PCBs), which is composed of two layers feeding networks and one layer radiating elements. For better expansibility and higher efficiency, full corporate substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feeding networks are specially designed and a 2×2-slot antenna subarray excited by higher order mode SIC is presented. Simulated results show that this 8×8 slot array achieves a maximum gain of 24.4 dBi and an impedance matching bandwidth of 34.75-35.75 GHz. High isolation above 50 dB is realized between the two input ports and cross polarization is under -30 dB. In addition, the aperture efficiency is 65%.

articleTitle: A special transmission characteristic of the electromagnetic wave in the plasma sheath surrounding a near-space vehicle and its analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The sheath flows surrounding a near-space blunt-cone vehicle at different speeds are simulated with FLUENT software. Analysis on the flow fields shows that, when the vehicle speed exceeds a certain threshold, the relationship between concentration and speed is opposite to that in low-speed state. Then, the Runge-Kutta method is applied to solve the EM ray equation in the inhomogeneous plasma sheath, in which the electron density at any point is calculated by the Lagrange interpolation method from the discrete simulation data of the flow field, and the electromagnetic wave propagation attenuation is obtained by segmentation integral combing with the EM theory. The results show that, when the vehicle speed is below a certain threshold, the energy transfer efficiency of EM waves decreases as the vehicle speed increases. On the contrary, for a vehicle speed greater than the threshold, the energy transfer efficiency will be enhanced with the speed increasing. This conclusion can help to understand the EM wave transmission characteristics in the plasma sheath around the hypersonic vehicle and provide a reference for the channel selection of the vehicle.

articleTitle: Tunable substrate integrated waveguide bandpass filter using liquid crystal material
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A microwave tunable substrate integrated waveguide bandpass filter using nematic liquid crystals is researched in this paper combined with the complementary split-ring resonators. The nematic liquid crystal is used to control the corresponding working frequency, with its permittivity changing caused by deflection angle of the liquid crystal molecules. And its deflection angle changing is controlled by the bias voltage. The simulation results show that the permittivity of liquid crystal changes from 2.79 to 3.56 to make the passband frequency achieve 490 MHz frequency offset.

articleTitle: An artificial anisotropy WCS-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, we present a three-dimensional (3-D) artificial anisotropy weakly conditional stability finite-difference time-domain (WCS-FDTD) method to achieve better dispersion performance. This artificial anisotropy WCS-FDTD algorithm can minimize the dispersion error for arbitrary incident angles and different time-step sizes. Stability analysis presents that this algorithm is weakly conditionally stable if proper artificial anisotropy parameter values are chosen. Dispersion analysis illustrates the error of the numerical phase velocity can be controlled.

articleTitle: Wideband polarization-independent anomalous reflection mediated by metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-thin metasurface is proposed to realize wideband polarization-independent anomalous reflection. The gradient metasurface is done by 6 discrete orientation of the local sub-wavelength resonator, which provides a phase gradient. The simulation and measured results show that 9 GHz bandwidth of the anomalous reflection is achieved.

articleTitle: Main beam angle control microstrip antenna based on phase gradient metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel main beam angle control microstrip antenna is designed and fabricated by loading a monolayer transmissive phase gradient metasurface (PGM). The anomalous refraction effects of the PGM are able to introduce predefined wave vector to control the radiation direction. The resonant frequencies of the four different PGM loaded antennas are kept at 9 GHz when the height of the cavity is fixed. However, different radiation deflection angles 0°, 9.5°, 18.7°, 27.2° are achieved and respond correspondingly to the implemented phase difference 0°, 10°, 20°, 30°. The thickness of the antenna is reduced to merely 0.1*wavelength. The measured results conform with the theoretical calculation and the simulated results, which indicates this design method is convincing and viable.

articleTitle: A compact quad-band bandstop filter using square spiral resonators based on folded stepped impedance resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, we propose the simulation, design and fabrication of the microstip quad-band bandstop filter (QBBSF) with Square Spiral Resonators (SSR). The basic cell of the structure consists of a folded stepped impedance microstrip transmission line. The center frequency of the filter is 1.12 GHz, 3.61 GHz, 6.20 GHz and 9.81GHz with the bandwidth of 1.13 GHz, 1.25 GHz, 1.12 GHz and 3.01GHz, respectively. The experimental results are closely matched with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Conformal multi-beam directional array antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper aims to design the low sidelobe microstrip array antenna with a certain angle beam which works in Ka-band. By controlling the difference feeding phase shift and space between the units, the beam angle is acquired. At the center frequency of 35 GHz for a patch, the bandwidth is 2.3 GHz, and the gain is 8.17 dBi; The bandwidth of array antenna is 1.54 GHz and the gain is 20.7 dBi, the beam offset-angle is 45°.

articleTitle: Using the finite difference parabolic equation with nonlocal boundary condition for complex environment radiowave propagation prediction
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the first time, we use the nonlocal boundary conditions in wide-angle finite difference parabolic equation model to calculate the propagation loss in complex environment. The great advantage of this method is that it has less amount of calculation without any loss of accuracy. The correctness and accuracy of this method are proved by using it to compute some propagation examples.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband polarization conversion metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a novel ultra-thin polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) that efficiently rotates linear polarization of electromagnetic waves is presented. The proposed PCM is consist of fish-bone shaped resonators. By the design with five resonances of the PCM unit cell, an ultra-wideband cross-polarization reflection is achieved. The simulation results show that the proposed PCM can realize more than 93% polarization conversion ratio (PCR) from 7.1GHz to 23.2GHz under both x-and y-polarized normal incidence. Compare to the published designs, the proposed metasurface has a compact profile and simple geometry but a high performance, and can be used in many areas like reflector antennas, radar stealth.

articleTitle: A low-profile broadband UHF base station antenna based on lumped-element matching network
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The paper has proposed a low-profile broadband UHF base station antenna based on lumped-element matching network with the combination of a height compressed conical antenna and a matching network. The proposed antenna is applied in base station communication systems with the frequency range from 300MHz to 870MHz. Compared with the traditional UHF base station antenna, the proposed antenna has a lower profile with the height of 80mm, only 0.08 λ at 300MHz. Consideration of high power, low-profile, bandwidth and radiation pattern, it's great to adopt a conical antenna with a matching network to constitute the proposed antenna. And the lumped-element inductances and capacitances are applied to constitute the broadband matching network, and the lumped-element is welded on surface of the copper plate that is 1.0mm thick. From the experimental results, the S11 of the antenna is almost less than −12dB in the frequency band, the directivity is about 4.15dBi, the elevation/depression angle is +70°/ −70° and has a great horizontal omnidirectional radiation pattern. The proposed antenna has a reference value to develop the associated UHF base station antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of a combined waveform of linear frequency modulation and phase coded modulation
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Phase coded modulation (PCM) waveform is highly Doppler sensitive. This paper studies a combined waveform called LF-PCM which adopts intra-pulse linear frequency modulation (LFM) to PCM to mitigate the impact of Doppler shift. LF-PCM is more Doppler robust than conventional PCM waveform, which makes it suitable for high speed target detection. Moreover, LF-PCM's two-dimensional Rang-Doppler resolution is finer than that of LFM waveform with equal bandwidth.

articleTitle: Low angle estimation with colored noise in bi-static MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to estimate the unknown angular location of a bi-static multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar target in the low angle scenario. The multipath model is formulated, in which the specular reflection is treated as an image target and the diffuse reflection is taken as spatial correlated stationary Gaussian noise. Based on this model, the colored noise is cancelled by covariance differencing approach first. Then the differencing array covariance matrix is reconstructed into a block Hankel matrix to differentiate coherent signals of the actual targets and image targets. A unitary ESPRIT algorithm is utilized to give the accurate low angle estimations with low computational burden at last. Simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis of antenna noise temperature measurement using Y-factor method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Measurement principle and procedure for the antenna noise temperature are represented simply by Y-factor method. Effect of uncertainties for ambient load and low-noise amplifier noise temperature on antenna noise temperature measurement is analyzed, and absolute error equation of antenna noise temperature measurement is derived. At fast, analysis and test examples of antenna noise temperature test error are given.

articleTitle: Quad-band microstrip antenna with only one slot on the edge
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A quad-band microstrip antenna is presented and experimentally studied for wireless local area network and the fourth generation mobile communication systems. The proposed antenna is fed by coaxial line and constructed by a slotted rectangular radiation patch. After the position of coaxial line is adjusted and an L-shaped slot is grooved around the edge of the patch, quad-band characteristic can be obtained at 1.94 GHz, 2.5 GHz, 3.1 GHz, and 3.4 GHz with bandwidth enough, and is suitable for frequency requirements above wireless systems. Antenna performances, influenced by the position of coaxial line, shape and size of the slot, are investigated by using electromagnetic simulation software. Experimental results are verified the properties of this design.

articleTitle: A compact Vivaldi antenna for wideband application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized Vivaldi antenna is presented. A Vivaldi antenna with a novel feeding structure is selected as the basic design and resistive loading is used at the end of it to make a compact structure. The proposed antenna is fabricated with the size of 140mm (length) *139mm (width)*1mm (thickness). The test results, which agree with the simulation results, indicate that the bandwidth is 0.44~3GHz (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10dB) and the gain ranges from -4.9dB to 7.70dB.

articleTitle: Thermal study of MOSFET under HEMP
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A simulator based on drift-diffusion physics model is used in this paper to study the electro-thermal response of MOSFET under HEMP by setting induced voltage signals to the electrode of the device. The temperature of the MOSFET rises if the amplitude of forward-biased induced signal is greater than threshold of the device and falls down either the induce signal is less than threshold or it is forward-biased. In heating process, heat generated by electro-thermal effect is concentrated in one end of the channel that close to drain electrode and makes it to be a hot-dot, while in cooling or heat conduction process, the distribution of temperature tends to be uniformity in the middle of the channel. The intense and acutely varying electric field in the hot-dot leads to the generation of Joule heat as numerical result shows and begets this position the vulnerability of MOSFET under HEMP interference. Simulation result can be applied in damage mechanism analysis and harden design of MOSFET against the HEMP.

articleTitle: General theory on electromagnetic scattering of an off-axis Hermite-Gaussian beam by a rotationally uniaxial anisotropic spheroid
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This letter presents a field expansion of the solution to three-dimensional electromagnetic scattering problems of a uniaxial anisotropic spheroidal particle illuminated by an off-axis Hermite-Gaussian (HG) beam. Using the complex-source-point method, and the relationship between spherical and spheroidal vector wave functions (VWFs), a method is put forward to expand the incident Hermite-Gaussian beam in terms of the spheroidal VWFs. By utilizing the complete relationship between spherical and spheroidal VWFs, the expansion formats of the EM fields in a uniaxial anisotropic spheroid in terms of the spheroidal vector wave functions are derived. The unknown expansion coefficients of the internal fields and scattered field are determined by applying the boundary conditions of the continuity of the tangential components of the electric and magnetic vectors across the surface of the spheroid. These theory works are hopeful to provide an effective test for further research on the numerical analysis of the interaction between a uniaxial anisotropic spheroid and laser beam.

Author Keywords: scattering anisotropic medium spheroid Hermite Gaussian beam

articleTitle: Analysis of Vivaldi antenna on cross-polarization application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper provides analysis of two classical Vivaldi antenna, which contains the characteristic of impedance matching in wideband, structure of antenna in height, especially the cross-polarization in E-plane and H-plane that is significant in dual-polarization array. Vivaldi antenna with dissymmetrical matching structure, is proposed with insupportable cross-polarization, though it has many excellent performance, such as wide-band, wide-scan, lower insertion loss and lower profile. This paper analysis the causation of the high cross-polarization in theory and the results are approved to be valid by simulating a trigonal array. It is important to check the element characteristic of cross-polarization in dual-polarization application.

articleTitle: MIMO channel sounder and millimeter wave measurements in a conference room
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Because of hundreds of megahertz bandwidth is a necessary condition for high speed data rates, the millimeter wave band will be used for 5G communication systems. Propagation channel measurements at mm-wave band were conducted in a conference room with an advanced MIMO channel sounder. An omnidirectional antenna at the transmitter and a horn antenna at the receiver were used. The transmitter antenna was fixed in one location while the receiver antenna was rotated 360 ° in azimuth in the measurement. The receiver antenna was conducted in 7.5° increments to capture measured data with eleven locations. The results of path loss and shadow fading factors are presented here using reference distance path loss model based on measured data.

articleTitle: Comparison of Taylor and Rachidi models for response calculation of field-to-line coupling
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper compares the similarities and differences of Taylor and Rachidi field-to-line coupling model and analyze the influencing factors of terminal response. Based on the transmission line theory, the model of two-wire transmission line excited by an incident plane wave is built, we compared the telegrapher's equations and exciting sources between these two models, then the BLT equation of load response is derived, and finally we discussed the relationship among terminal load induced voltage, conductor separation, line length and irradiation frequency.

articleTitle: An ultra-broadband THz absorber based on graphene
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The development of modern radar technology has a great threat to the stealth of military targets such as aircrafts. Absorber can be used to enhance the stealth of military targets. In this paper, an ultra-broadband THz absorber based on graphene is proposed. The absorption rate over 90% is from 0.48THz to 1.82THz and the relative absorption bandwidth is 117%. Then the absorbing mechanism of the absorber is analyzed by the method of impedance matching. The results show the validity of the simulation. Moreover, the absorber has excellent properties of insensitive polarization and wide incident angle range.

articleTitle: A novel, dual-band, miniaturized antenna with fractal-curve patch and TSV-CPW feeder
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The miniaturization of antenna is critical to the performance of RF-SiP. This paper presents the design and fabrication of a novel, miniaturized antenna that uses a fractal structure. The antenna has two resonate frequencies at 24GHz and 35GHz, respectively. Unlike a rectangular patch antenna, the patch of the proposed antenna is shaped similarly to a Peano curve and uses a Through Silicon Via-Coplanar Waveguide (TSV-CPW) as a feeder. The area of the Peano-curve patch is the smallest for a given perimeter. The simulation results describing the return loss, and the dual-band performance can be realized by loading this type of fractal structure. Finally, the proposed antenna may be applicable in multi-chip packaging and related integrated passive modules.

articleTitle: Design of a dual(UHF/S) bands antenna handset
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual(UHF/S) bands handset antenna is designed in this paper. On S(1.9-2.2GHz) band, a quadrifilar helix is used to get the circular polarization, and a monopole antenna is for UHF(420-520MHz) band. The two antennas are arranged in a coaxial with the same axle. The measured results show the antenna's results is agree with the simulation ones.

articleTitle: Low-profile double-frequency Fabry-Perot (F-P) cavity antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new electromagnetic metamaterial unit cell of multiband frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed in this paper. The new unit cell consists of meander line on one side of a substrate. It is shown that the structure exhibits a negative reflection phase property and Strong reflection characteristic at 1.9GHz and 2.44GHz. A 6×8 array of these unit cells (FSS screen) is used as a superstrate at a distance λ/24(center frequency) over a multiband patch antenna. Gain improvement of 5 dBi at 1.9GHz and 4.1dBi at 2.44GHz respectively, as the patch antenna with FSS superstrate compared to the patch antenna without superstrate.

articleTitle: A narrow-angle parabolic equation model in atmospheric ducts
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the narrow-angle parabolic equation (NAPE) model applied on atmospheric ducts is solved by using the improved discrete mixed Fourier transform (IDMFT) method which is an efficient form of the split-step Fourier transform (SSFT) algorithm under the impedance boundary conditions. In order to verify the accuracy of the narrow-angle parabolic equation method, the numerical results are compared with the experimental data in the literature as well as the results of mode theory and the Advanced Refractive Effects Prediction System (AREPS) software. Finally, the effects of the receiving antenna height and the evaporation duct height on the propagation loss in the evaporation duct are analyzed in details.

articleTitle: Modeling of three-dimensional weak magnetic field induced by water movement
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the Weaver's model and Neumann ocean waves spectrum, the three-dimensional space of the three-dimensional random waves and three-dimensional model of the magnetic field generated by water movement are simulated in this paper. This paper provides a weak magnetic field reference model for the magnetic detection of long distance underwater magnetic object.

Author Keywords: three-dimensional model of the magnetic field

articleTitle: Design of a W band filter antenna array with low sidelobe level using gap waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Gap waveguide (GW) was investigated to realize low loss millimeter wave (mm-wave) transmission line in recent years. In this paper, groove gap waveguide (GGW) is used to design a W band filter antenna array. A 14 slots antenna array with a center fed structure and a fourth order cavity bandpass filter are designed respectively. Then the method of integration is used in the combining of antenna and filter to eliminate the transition loss between the two parts. Simulation result shows an antenna gain of 18.64dBi and a side lobe level (SLL) of 20.64dB at the center frequency 94.55GHz. Interference signal outside the frequency range 92.8-96.3GHz is compressed efficiently in our design.

articleTitle: Modified Doherty power amplifier based on asymmetrical load matching networks
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel deep back-off Doherty power amplifier based on asymmetrical load matching networks is proposed in this paper. The asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (ADPA) modulates carrier power amplifier (PA)'s load impedance in peak output power region. With the optimized matching method and modulation mode, the ADPA achieves optimum efficiency across the whole output back-off (OBO) power region. Due to the novel asymmetric load matching networks, the structure of output power combiner also gets simplified. The enhanced performance is implemented by the ADPA built with CREE's GaN HEMT CGH40010 and CGH40025 devices at 2.6GHz. Measurement results show the proposed ADPA can achieve 55.3% power added efficiency (PAE) at 9.2dB back-off power level and a favorable ACPR of-53.7dBc.

articleTitle: Design of miniaturized WLAN notched ultra-wideband microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A miniaturized ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna has been designed. It is used for the WLAN with notched band. A circle slot is etched on the radiation patch; a cross strip line is added in the middle of patch. This structure makes antenna with the effect of notch, which can effectively restrain narrowband spectrum interference with WLAN. Using the electromagnetic simulation software, the miniaturized size of antenna structure is carried out. Fabricated sample verifies that the antenna can be suitable for the requirement of notched UWB application.

articleTitle: A low-RCS microstrip antenna using EBG and HIS structure
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel method aimed at reducing radar cross section (RCS) of microstrip antenna is presented in this paper. The stopband electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) is used to replace the metallic ground of the proposed antenna to reduce the out-of-band RCS. Meanwhile, the high impedance surface (HIS) is applied to reduce RCS in the operation frequency by canceling out the reflected wave. Thus, a wideband RCS reduction can be realized in and out of antenna's operating frequency band. Results indicate that in-band RCS is reduced as much as 2.5 dB compared to the reference antenna. At the same time, out-of-band RCS is reduced due to the EBG structure, and has a maximum RCS reduction value of 19 dB. The whole band of RCS reduction is from 2 GHz to 15 GHz. With distinct low-RCS characteristic and little effect on radiation performance, the proposed method will have an extensive application on designing antenna with a requirement of RCS control.

articleTitle: A C-band 16×16 array antenna for microwave communication
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For miniaturization the microwave communication equipment, a miniaturized and low cost array antenna is proposed. A 2-layer of patch antenna unit is designed to broaden the bandwidth of the microstrip antenna. The CST MWS is used to simulate and optimize the antenna structure. Based on the designed antenna unit, an array antenna is proposed to achieve high gain, and the simulation and optimization are conducted. The array antenna prototype is fabricated on dielectric substrate by using PCB processing technic based on the simulation results. And the measurement for the array antenna is carried out, the measured results can be coincide with the simulation, the gain of the antenna is about 27dBi, and the S11 parameter of the antenna is less than -10dB in the frequency range.

articleTitle: On the radar detection analysis under the interference environment based on the Monte Carlo method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The method combining Monte Carlo method and MATLAB is presented to analyze the radar detection performance under the interference environment. The Monte Carlo method which is validated firstly to prove to have the same accuracy as the analytical method is ideal to analyze radar detection performance under the interference environment. The Monte Carlo method is utilized to analyze radar detection performance under the interference environment when multiple interference signals are inputted. The radar output distribution characteristics and are false alarm ration analyzed.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband terahertz reflective polarization conversion based on anisotropic meta-mirror with interlaced-parallel-dipole metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband, high efficiency, and wide angle terahertz reflective polarization converter (RPC) using interlaced-parallel-dipole metamaterial (IPDMM) is theoretically demonstrated in this paper. Illuminated by linearly polarized (LP) wave, the proposed polarizer performances an excellent 90° linear polarized conversions at three resonance frequencies, and pure circularly polarized (CP) conversion at two resonance frequencies. Remarkably, due to the enhanced inductive-capacitive (LC) resonances by the IPDMM using double-parallel cut-wire particles, 99% ultra-broadband width of triple-band overlapping over 75% and 0.99 highest power conversion efficiency are obtained numerically. Furthermore, the excellent cross-polarization conversion sustains when the incidence is a CP wave. In addition, the proposed polarizer obtains 80% relevant bandwidth over 70% reflective polarization conversion power with incident angle up to 45°. The physical mechanism of the polarization conversion is elucidated by analysis of the surface current distributions of the polarizer. The merits of broadband, high efficiency and widely incident angles could benefit the potential applications in THz regime.

articleTitle: Designing a radome with frequency selective surface by using the physical optics method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a hemispheric radome with conformal frequency selective surface is designed and analyzed by using the physical optics method. The conformal frequency selective surface consists of two layers of substrate and three layers of periodic patches and grids. The radome is manufactured and measured. The comparison between the analysis result of the physical optics method and the experimental result show that they are agree very well, which verify that the physical optics method is an effective method for calculating the electrical large structures.

articleTitle: Broadband vertically/horizontally dual-polarized antenna for base stations
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband vertically/horizontally (V/H) dual-polarized antenna is proposed for mobile communication base stations. The V/H dual-polarized antenna consists of two perpendicularly placed dual-dipole elements. By shaping the reflector for V/H dual-polarized antenna, a half-power beam width of 65+8° is achieved for both vertical and horizontal polarizations. The V/H dual-polarized antenna has a bandwidth of 48% (1.7-2.75 GHz) for return loss>15 dB. An 8-element V/H dual-polarized antenna array is also developed.

articleTitle: Retrieving the troposphere duct by using ground-based radiometric profiler in South Coast in China
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Coastal areas worldwide are known to be especially `rich' in super refractive layers and waveguides that affect microwave propagation. Radiosonde data of Xiamen and Haikou in south coast in China were chosen to analysis the rule and characteristics of the troposphere duct in this paper. Based on the historical data, improved learning vector quantization neural network method (LVQ) and improved Radial Basis Function neural network method (RBF) is used to retrieving the troposphere duct. The two algorithms are presented by using the brightness temperature detected by the ground-based multi-channel microwave radiometer both in zenith and gradient angles. Feasibility of this method is demonstrated with the results by the measure data. Ground-based multi-channel microwave radiometer has been proven to be a powerful tool to sensing troposphere duct, which can perform continuous troposphere duct profiles and provide information of electromagnetism environment for the application of radar, communication and navigation systems.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-band combined Mic-dip antenna for wireless communication applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band combined Mic-Dip antenna (Microstrip antenna and Dipole antenna) is proposed in this paper. The combined antenna, including the microstip antenna and the dipole antenna, is working for lower and upper band, respectively. To widen impedance bandwidth for the two operation bands, the coupling feed is employed for Mic-Dip antenna, which can achieve operating bandwidth of about 9.14 % ranging from 2.318-2.54 GHz for lower band and about 36.7 % ranging from 5.158-7.48 GHz for upper band (VSWR ≤ 2). By reusing the radiation patch of the microstip antenna as the reflector of the dipole, the low profile is obtained. The compact dimension of the antenna, by shorting the radiation patch of the microstrip antenna to the ground plane, is further achieved. In addition, the favorable consistency of the radiation patterns in the whole operated bands are realized by using combined antenna. The isolation of more than 25 dB can be achieved between two ports in the required bands. With these good performances, the antenna is very suitable for indoor wireless communication system applications.

articleTitle: A dual-band microstrip antenna for aviation and mobile application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band microstrip antenna is designed for aviation and mobile application. It is using the slot loading technique and the short-sheet loading technique. Grooving an L-shaped slot on radiation patch. It can change the original current path and form two relatively independent current loops, the antenna works at 1 GHz and 2.48 GHz. The minimum return loss at 1 GHz is -32.28 dB and at 2.48 GHz is -14.48 dB. Both of two working frequencies have enough bandwidth, and can meet the frequency requirements of aviation navigation systems and of Compass Navigation Satellite System efficiently. This design is analyzed by electromagnetic simulation software, and measured results show the effectiveness of it.

articleTitle: Terahertz multi-band reflective polarization converter based on TSRR metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we have theoretically proposed a planar, four-band linearly and circularly reflective polarizer using two splits ring resonant (TSRR) metamaterial. The proposed reflective polarizer can convert a linearly polarized wave to its cross-polarized wave at four resonant frequencies, and can also convert the linearly polarized wave to circularly polarized wave at other five resonant frequencies. The physical mechanism behind the phenomena is elucidated by simulating surface current distributions of the unit cell structure. Besides, the multi-band reflective polarizer can become a broadband one by increasing the dielectric thickness. With simple geometry, high efficiency, the reflective polarizer has huge potential for application in terahertz regime.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized cross dipole with wide beam for satellite-borne application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband cross dipole with circular polarization and wide beam was presented for satellite-borne application. It consists of two rectangular orthogonal dipoles, a circular parasitic plate, and a grooved ground plane. This proposed antenna is designed to work from 2GHz to 5GHz. Its dimension is Φ1.08λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> × 0.41λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is the wavelength of center frequency. The parasitic plate and grooved ground plane were proved to be capable in gain enhancement within ±60° radiation beam in the whole operating band, especially from 4GHz to 5GHz. Its measured circularly polarized gains are all above 2.6dBic within ±45° radiation beam, meanwhile, the axial ratio is less than 3dB. This proposed antenna has compact structure and easy to be fabricated, which is suitable for satellite-borne application.

articleTitle: A new compact edge coupled filter-antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new filter-antenna for wireless communication was described in this paper. The printed antenna was integrated with a edge coupled filter to get the lower insertion loss. The measured results show that the antenna can operate on 2.34GHz ~ 2.80GHz with good radiation pattern. The gain of antenna is between -1dBi and 3.37dBi.

articleTitle: Coupling reduction of closely packed antennas by stringing EBG structure
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A stringing Electromagnetic ban-gap (S-EBG) structure is proposed in this paper for coupling reduction of microstrip antenna array. The The S-EBG is constructed by interlinking three mushroom-type EBG in a line with a strip. While in the antenna element assembling direction, it is only one period and maintains a compact array. The structure is easy fabrication, assembling and no etching in the ground plane. A reference microstrip antenna array (RMAA), one conventional mushroom-type (CMT-EBG) element loaded microstrip antenna array (O-CMT-EBG-LMAA), and three CMT-EBG elements loaded microstrip antenna array (T-CMT-EBG-LMAA) were also studied. Research found over 20 dB coupling reduction is achieved by the S-EBG. Thus, the proposed S-EBG is good candidate for array coupling reduction.

articleTitle: Influence of atmospheric duct on low-angle radar tracking errors
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To investigate the problem of errors for radar tracking low angle target, based on the method of angle tracking and the parabolic equation, a suite of simulated results of elevation errors is presented. The errors of elevation angle have been calculated in conditions including evaporation duct, surface duct, and duct profiles changed with range, which demonstrate that the variation of atmospheric refraction can affect the errors of elevation angle associated with the multipath effects seriously. It means the atmospheric refraction is also a key factor to be considered in low-angle tracking.

articleTitle: Experimental research on multiple stages EMP protection measure for HF transmitter
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper experimental research was made to investigate the effect of multiple stages EMP (electromagnetic pulse) protection measure based on SG (spark gap) and GDT (gas discharge tube). The result showed that the advantages of measure were large current conduction capability and simple structure. In the case of incident pulse amplitude equal to 40kV, the residual pulse amplitude was less than 1kV. The drawback of the measure was that the breakdown voltage of spark gap was unstable and would not achieve good repeatability.

articleTitle: Improvement of the radiation and impedence performance for the SIW H-plane horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the impedance matching and radiation performance of the SIW H-plane horn antenna is improved by the modification of the probe and the adoption of a capacitive post in the feeding structure. The simulation results show that using the capacitive post and the modified probe, the reflection coefficient can be reduced, and the gain of the design can be improved in H-plane in the operation bandwidth from 27 GHz to 35.5 GHz as a result of the more uniform phase distribution at the radiation aperture.

articleTitle: 2D-DOA estimation for uniform rectangular array using noncircular HOSVD method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the problem of two-dimensional direction-of-arrival (2D-DOA) estimation for uniform rectangular array (URA). A noncircular high-order singular value decomposition (NC-HOSVD) is developed for 2D-DOA estimation. By employing the NC property of the source matrix as well as the multidimensional structure of the received data, an expanded three-order tensor model is formulated, which doubles the number of detectable sources. A signal subspace method is constructed to obtain 2D-DOA with the HOSVD method. The proposed NC-HOSVD method outperforms the ESPRIT and the HOSVD methods. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The difference in variation characteristics of the F2-peak height hmF2 at the low and middle latitudes
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: There is a continuing requirement for simple, but representative methods for determining the height of maximum electron concentration of the F2-layer (symbol hmF2), both for communication and navigation. The techniques for estimating the F2-peak height hmF2 from M(3000)F2 are reviewed with particular stress put upon those in which the effects of underlying ionization are accounted for by a correction to M(3000)F2, formulated in terms of the ratio f0F2 and f0E. Changes in the neutral atmosphere and in the hmF2 model have minor effects at low latitudes, where the fluxes are larger, but can appreciably alter the results at middle latitudes.
