At 21° latitude, neutral winds have a major effect on the distribution of ionization from the equatorial fountain. Thus, at the solstices the day-time flow is about 4 times larger in winter than summer. This paper reports on a comparison of the difference in variation characteristics of the observed monthly mean ionospheric F2-peak height hmF2 at Lanzhou (36.06°N latitude) and Haikou (20°N latitude) for both solar minimum (2005-2007) and solar maximum (2010-2011). The diurnal, seasonal, and solar variation of the hmF2 at the two sites compared with results of detailed calculations. Also, the contemporary practical implementations will be compared and contrasted in the light of this investigation and the scope for further refinements will be discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering for multilayered spheres induced by laser sheet beam
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Laser sheet is of great practical importance in various fields, such as particle image velocimetry and probe detections. On the contrary to Gaussian beam, laser sheet is the beam focused by a cylindrical lens. In order to better understand the physical mechanism, the paper is devoted to the description of the interaction between a multilayered sphere and a laser sheet beam by using the generalized Lorenz-Mie Theory (GLMT). Comparisons among the scattering properties of laser sheet, Gaussian beam and plane wave are carried out.

articleTitle: Study on the absorption properties of a curved metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We investigate the absorption properties of a curved metamaterial absorber (CMA) in microwave. The simulation results show that the CMA could be used with better performance than the traditional planar metamaterial absorber (PMA) with the same physical parameters in exciting more perfect absorption peaks. Moreover, the absorption properties are related to the polarization direction of electromagnetic (EM) waves, which make it possible for the CMA to be used as frequency selective absorber. In addition, the effects of structure parameters of the unit cell on absorption properties are analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival estimation for monostatic MIMO radar using reduced-dimension RISR algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the issue of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for monostatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar is investigated, and a new reduced-dimensional re-iterative superresolution (RD-RISR) algorithm for DOA estimation is proposed based upon a recursive implementation of minimum mean-square error (MMSE) framework. In the proposed algorithm, a reduced-dimensional matrix is employed to transform the data matrix into a low dimensional space. Afterwards, the DOA is estimated via the RISR algorithm. The proposed algorithm has the benefits of intrinsic determination of model order, enable "tracking" of sources with low sample support, and robustness to coherent sources such as can occur in multipath environments. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-band microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces the design method of a dual band microstrip patch antenna, from the most basic of microstrip patch method using bilateral radiation, a dual band microstrip antenna is designed, simulated using HFSS software, results show that, choose a 50 ohm coaxial cable feed position to make the antenna work at the center frequency respectively in 9.96GHz 12.84GHz. And in the 9.96GHz and 12.84GHz echo loss to minimum, bandwidths are respectively 270MHz and 550MHz, antenna has good dual-band resonance characteristics.

articleTitle: Ultra broadband metamaterial absorber with oblique incidence based on effective medium theory
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We demonstrate the design, measurement, retrieval effective parameters and calculations of an ultra-broad band metamaterial absorber (MMA), in which the metallic resonant structures including the inserted chip resisters and the substrate are equivalent to a homogeneous and isotropic effective medium. The effective electromagnetic (EM) parameters are retrieved by extracting the reflected and transmitted coefficients, and absorbance of the MMA is calculated by the retrieved effective EM parameters based on effective medium theory. The calculated results are in good agreement with simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: The statistic and analysis of atmospheric ducts worldwide using radiosonde data
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study analyzed atmospheric ducts occurrence using radiosonde data obtained from 2005 to 2014 worldwide. The results show that the probabilities of ducting occurrence vary in different regions all over the world. The average year occurrences of surface ducts decrease gradually with the increase of latitude. And, comparisons of the duct distribution between the land and sea show that, the occurrence rate of marine is higher than that of land. At last, a comparison between ducting occurrences obtained from Rec. ITU-R P. 453-11 and this statistics has been made in this contribution.

Author Keywords: the gradient of the modified refractivity

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for volume integral equation using interpolative decomposition and multilevel fast multipole algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The fast algorithm which combines interpolative decomposition (ID) and the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is extended to the method of moments (MoM) solution of volume integral equations (VIE) from that of surface integral equations (SIE). Boxes in the finest level in MLFMA are further divided and the rank-deficient submatrices of the near-field interactions are approximated by the data sparse representation through the ID. Numerical experiments are conducted to study the performance of the fast solver.

articleTitle: Design of the top-loaded quadrifilar helix antenna for low profile applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low profile quadrifilar helix antenna based on top-loaded technology for global navigation satellite system is presented in this paper. The top-loaded technology can both be used to reduce the profile of the wire form quadrifilar helix antenna and the printed form. An S-band top-loaded quadrifilar helix antenna has been simulated and possesses the characteristic of wide beam width, high gain at the low elevation, good circular polarization performance and the low profile. This low profile antenna can be an attractive candidate for handset applications.

articleTitle: Broadband microwave propagation in a novel large volume glow discharge argon plasma
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The broadband microwave propagating characteristics of a novel, large volume, glow-discharge argon plasma is reported in this paper. A large volume, glow-discharge argon plasma was designed and the basic plasma parameters were determined using an Impedans Ltd. Langmuir probe under a variety of conditions. The transmission attenuation was recorded by using S parameters of a vector network analyzer with the frequency range from 2GHz to 18GHz and a propagation model was established using the Z transform FDTD method for simulating the attenuation of microwave. The effects of both the gas pressure and input power on the EM wave propagation are analyzed. The results showed that the theoretical and experimental results of transmission attenuation were in good agreement. Moreover, the electron density n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> and the effective collision rate v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> were found to play important roles in the propagation of microwave.

articleTitle: Extraction of distributed capacitance for microstrip lines using conformal technique based on finite-difference method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method using conformal technique of finite-difference method (FDM) is proposed to solve the distributed capacitance for microstrip lines. Instead of deriving the average dielectric constant ε, this method uses electric field numerical weights to process the inhomogeneous cells, and takes the discontinuous effects of both inhomogeneous Ampere cell and Faraday cell into account. The new method shows good agreement with the measurement and traditional methods.

articleTitle: Two designs of bidirectional same-sense circularly polarized antennas with cavity structures
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Two antennas with bidirectional same-sense circularly polarization are presented in this paper. The first antenna consists two back-to-back patches with a common ground and a stepped microstrip feeding line. The two patches are behaving as a cavity by coupling through a slot on the common ground, providing bidirectional patterns with the same-sense circular polarization. Based on the dual-patch cavity structure, another cavity antenna with crossed slots on the front and back sides are proposed as the second antenna, also providing bidirectional circular polarization with the same sense. Especially, the second antenna is designed on both sides of only one layer of substrate, with the merits of low cost and easy fabrication. By numerical simulation, we studied the bandwidth and axial ratio properties of two proposed antenna with cavity structures.

articleTitle: A study of electromagnetic scattering from sea surface with breaking waves using generalized forward-backward method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The generalized forward-backward method was used to investigate the scattering characteristics from the sea surface with breaking waves, which gives a preliminary analysis of mechanism of sea spike phenomenon. The integral equation using impedance boundary condition was used for one-dimensional (1-D) PM surface. GFBM increasingly improved the computational efficiency and made it possible to calculate rapidly electromagnetic scattering from sea surface at low grazing angles. The results show that there are larger fluctuations of the scattering intensity with the effects of the breaking waves in HH polarization than that in VV polarization.

articleTitle: Multiband plasmonic filter based on double layer spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, a multi-band plasmonic filter based on double layer spoof surface plasmon polaritons was presented. The multi-band performance resulted from the high-order modes of the spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs), which has been verified through the dispersion curves and surface electric fields. The cutoff frequency of each band of the filter corresponded to different order of modes of the asymptotic frequency of the SSPPs, which could be tuned by the depth of the groove at will. This simple multi-band plasmonic filter has potential applications in plasmonic circuits and systems.

articleTitle: Investigation on down-conductor system layout for electronic equipment protection
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Lightning currents and LEMP radiation field may destroy electronic equipments. External lightning protection system provides protection for outdoor and indoor equipments from the direct lightning flash. The extremely high induced ground voltage and electromagnetic radiation, generated by the lightning current flowing on air-termination and down-conductor system are harmful to nearby electronic equipments. Electrical fields and magnetic fields in different down-conductor layouts are simulated in this paper, and beneficial down-conductors symmetry layout project of lightning protection system is investigated to reduce the harm of lightning current.

articleTitle: Effect of discontinuous snow coverage on radiation characteristics of the leaky rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In urban mass transit railway system, the leaky rectangular waveguide is continuously mounted along the track, for both under- and on-ground environments, to realize a reliable wireless communication between trains and ground. The performance of the waveguide on ground is easily affected by the bad weather, especially for the heavy snowing weather. The available works only considered the effect of the continuous snow coverage on the whole waveguide. In this paper, the effect of discontinuously covering snow on the near field characteristics of the leaky rectangular waveguide is analyzed. Then an effective way for reducing the influence is proposed, in which a dielectric layer is used to cover the waveguide. By this method, stable distribution of electric field can be achieved.

articleTitle: Motion compensation for high range resolution profile based on stepped-frequency waveforms
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In stepped-frequency radar systems, target motions produce range-profile distortions. The velocity of the target induces range shift, signal-to-noise ratio loss, range profile spreading, so it should be compensated. The conventional technology requires velocity estimation. In this paper, we propose a new way to eliminate or suppress the distortion of the synthetic range profile. This technique combines two pulse bursts which satisfy certain mathematical relationship and is also easier to implement. The simulation results of this paper show the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: One method to improve gain of holographic surface antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Holographic surface antennas have aroused huge attention in last several years for the characteristics of high gain, low profile and easily fabrication. Many works have been done in this field. However, for the traditional holographic surface antenna, there is always a split in the main lobe direction of radiation pattern. In order to eliminate the split in the main lobe direction, we combine two parts of holographic surface with impedance modulation function out of phase in the and regions. By applying this technique, the realized gain of holographic surface antenna is improved about 15dBi in the desired direction.

articleTitle: A new measurement of atmospheric coherent length using differential image motion
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric coherence length indicated the intensity of turbulence has the characteristics of regional and temporal variations. Real-time measuring the change of atmospheric coherence length and grasping its rules is a primary job for researching on laser propagation in atmosphere. In view of the deficiency of the existing measurement method in portability and economy, a new measurement of atmospheric coherent length using electronic eyepiece and image processing is proposed. The error factors of experiment system are analyzed, and the feasibility of the method is proved with the aid of the data gained from temperature fluctuation instrument. Finally, the characteristics of atmospheric turbulence in Guilin are analyzed using the experiment results.

articleTitle: Multi-sleeve monopole antenna for APP-terminal communication
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new multi-sleeve monopole antenna for APP-terminal communication is proposed and compared with the conventional sleeve monopole antenna. The prototype of the proposed antenna is constructed and simulated, which shows that the proposed antenna features excellent radiation characteristics against the working frequency, where the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is less than 1.5.

articleTitle: The recognition method based on the height of the reentry target
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To solve the problem that the Mass-to-Drag Ratio of the reentry target can't be extracted stably, a recognition method based on the height when the velocity of reentry target declines is proposed. The method extracts the height when the velocity of reentry target declines, because the air resistance on the light and heavy target is different. Then these two kinds of target with different Mass-to-Drag Ratio can be distinguished. Simulation examples show that the proposed feature is easier and more intuitive than the Mass-to-Drag Ratio, and it is verified to be a stable and valid characteristic.

articleTitle: Analysis of scattering characteristics of 3-D objects with rough surfaces
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The split-and-project method is introduced to modeling the 3D objects with rough surfaces. With this method, the blunt-nosed cone (BNC) and delta-wing aircraft (DWA) are taken as examples to build the rough objects. The bi-static RCS of the rough objects are then simulated through Physical Optics (PO) method under different correlation length and root-mean-square (rms) height. Results indicate that the correlation length matters more than the latter on the RCS and DWA is more susceptible to the roughness of the surface.

articleTitle: The array design of the distributed space-based radar based on sunflower arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Spaced-based radar (SBR) systems have plenty of advantages, and it can provide both ground-moving-target indicator (GMTI) and airborne-moving-target indicator(AMT) data. The distributed arrays are attractive to SBR because they provide a high angular resolution with a long baseline. Also, they can inherently adopt small identical independent spacecrafts as sub-arrays. However, the distance between adjacent satellites is far more than half a wavelength, which arouse problems of grating lobes and high side lobes to the array synthesis. In this paper, the angular parameter of sunflower arrays is optimized using exhaustive method, furthermore, an non-uniform sparse array composed of small satellites is designed for the distributed space-based radar (DSBR) based on the sunflower array.

articleTitle: Simulation of asymmetry incoherent scatter spectra with the ion acoustic wave
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Under the condition of parametric decay instability excitation, the measured up-shifted ion line is higher than downshifted one. We are based on the assumption of the existence of ion acoustic velocity particles, a new ion velocity distribution function and incoherent scatter theory model with the PDI mechanism are build, and the spectra asymmetry characteristic of PDI is simulated successfully, which is consistent with experiments observations. It is great significance to understand the instability mechanism.

articleTitle: Study of a hybrid antenna consists of solid and liquid materials
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An antenna with both solid dielectric and liquid materials is designed and analyzed. The influence of the thickness and parameters of the substrate is investigated. The performance of different liquid materials including sea water, oil and distilled water is analyzed. The influence of the distribution of the liquid and other relevant factors are studied. The simulation results revealed the validity and flexibility of the combination of solid dielectric resonators and liquid ones.

articleTitle: Mitigation of RF blackout in plasma sheaths communication via nonlinear effects
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A mechanism of communication through plasma sheaths which surround vehicles traveling at hypersonic velocities is introduced. The idea is to use nonlinear effects to make the plasma sheath appear transparent.

articleTitle: A method to calculate the statistic characters of the transient electromagnetic pulse coupling into stochastic transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an improved method based on the Gauss-Legendre quadrature and Unscented Transform (UT) is proposed to estimate the statistical characters of the EMC/EMI problems with stochastic parameters. The UT method provides a fast method to propagate mean and covariance information through nonlinear transformations. The Gauss-Legendre quadrature as an efficient numerical integral method is used to select the sigma points and weights. The coupling problem of electromagnetic field and transmission line can be treated as a nonlinear maping. So, we calculate the statistical characters of coupling voltage on the load of the transmission line by the GLUT method. It only needs about five times of FDTD simulation to obtain the mean and standard deviation of the coupling voltage. The Monte Carlo (MC) method has been used to validate the GLUT method. The numerical simulation results indicate that the GL-UT method can reduce the number of FDTD simulation from more than thousands of times to several times.

articleTitle: Rainfall observation based on the VHF radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper shows some observations which indicate the VHF (Very High Frequency) radar is capable to observe simultaneously the echoes from rain particles and atmospheric turbulences in the rainfall environment. It is helpful to understand the precipitation mechanism and study the microphysical processes of rainfall at the whole heights.

articleTitle: A double-layer miniaturized dual band frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel double layer Dual Band Frequency Selective Surface (FSS)with miniaturized element is presented, in which each periodic cell consists of parallel metallic patch of two different sizes. The FSS with such structure is designed, The simulated results show that the FSS dimension is miniaturized to 0.06 λ (λ refers to the resonant wavelength of 2GHz). In addition, it also has good stability to oblique incidence waves for both TE and TM polarization, and there is no other resonance frequency up to 10 GHz. The influence of dimension parameters on FSS performances has been investigated. Then, dual-band FSS operated at 2GHz and 3.45GHz is designed. Simulated results indicate that the miniaturized FSS also provides good transmission response.

articleTitle: An analytic solution for double scattering of urban structures
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Double scattering between building and surrounded environment play an important role in the electromagnetic scattering model of urban. In the past, double scattering of vertical wall and rough surface has been studied, in this paper, a closed form solution based on geometrical optics (GO) between non-vertical wall and rough surface is derived. Physical optics (PO) can also be derived in the same way. The simulated data well matches the expected. At the same time, wall slope angle affects the double scattering distinctively. The obtained closed form can be employed in synthetic aperture radar image.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering characteristics of ablation rough surface in plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the four scattering paths method and Monte Carlo method for two dimensional rough surfaces, a rough surface model under the effect of ablation in the plasma sheath is established and the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the aircraft's rough surface covered by layered plasma media including ablation particles is calculated. The calculation results show that the single scattering electromagnetic field from the rough surface occupies the major part and the scattering coefficient in the specular reflection direction exhibits a scattering peak. The peak enhanced as the density and size of the ablation particles increases. Moreover, the denudation of the aircraft surface increases the surface roughness that obviously reduces scattering coefficient in the direction of specular reflection. This model could provide data support for the scattering analysis of hypersonic vehicles under the influence of ablation in the plasma sheath.

articleTitle: High-gain spoof surface plasmon polariton planar antenna based on the phase gradient metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, we propose a high-gain planar antenna based on the phase gradient metasurface whose super cell is composed of six different H-shaped elements. The metasurface can not only couple the y-polarized incident wave into spoof surface plasmon polariton but also achieve the reverse process when the splitter feed provides appropriate field and wave vector. The antenna works well that the return loss maintains lower than -10 dB from 9.5 GHz to 10.5 GHz. The beam pointing angle at 10 GHz is 16° which agrees well with the theoretical value.

articleTitle: Ka band small dual reflector antenna fed by dielectric rod antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high efficient electrically small dual reflector antenna is designed and measured. A dielectric rod antenna(DRA) is used as the feed of the dual reflector antenna, due to its advantages of narrow beam, high gain and radiates a rotationally symmetric radiation pattern. Simulations and measurements show that the maximum efficiency of 62.5% is achieved for a main reflector with only 12 wavelengths.

articleTitle: Designing and simulation of a ZigBee-communication printed circuit board
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The designing process of a ZigBee-Communication PCB (Printed Circuit Board) is presented. The layer-stack structure and through-hole structure for PCB via hole and pad are modelled firstly in HFSS simulation environment, and then the key designing parameters which affect the RF performance are identified and determined by simulation. The simulation result shows the PCB achieves -20dB return loss in the 2.4GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic coupling between concave layout array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It is a trend to replace the traditional discrete antenna with the array plane antenna, and the new electromagnetic interference problem produced by the array plane antenna is also the focus of the current research. This paper uses both simulation and experiments to research the issue about suppression of electromagnetic interference under the condition of two array plane antenna be laid in same plane. By means of simulation, the inhibitory effect of electromagnetic coupling between two array planes and the radiation characteristics of array plane antenna are studied on condition of concave/non-concave layout. In the laboratory environment, the inhibitory effect of electromagnetic coupling between two array planes on condition of concave/non-concave layout is studied by using the small array plane. The results show that the radiation characteristics of the antenna can not be affected by the concave layout array plane antenna, and the isolation between two array planes can be promoted by 5 dB.

articleTitle: The study of bandwidth and dual-band for near field broadband electric field coupling antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The near-field broadband electric field coupling antenna has many remarkable advantages, such as simple operation, safe connection and high efficient transmission of large capacity data. In recent years, it has been widely used in many fields. The TranferJet™ antenna mentioned in this paper is a typical representative of the high-speed near-field wireless technology. The target of broadening bandwidth and dual-band has been come true by transforming the form of the micro-strip line and coupled electrode. It shows the performance of the improved antenna employing 3D electromagnetic simulation software to simulate.

articleTitle: Wideband two bowtie dipole array antenna integrated with a tapered balun
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband antenna consisting of two series-fed fan-shaped bowtie dipole antenna elements and an integrated tapered balun for through-the-wall imaging radar (TWIR) applications. The two fan-shaped bowtie dipole antenna elements with different radii and same flare angle are connected using a coplanar stripline and backed by a ground reflector. The balun realized by a tapered microstrip line and a slot line is used to feed the antenna. The proposed antenna has been numerically investigated, which shows that a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 85.9% ranging from 1.38 to 3.46 GHz is attained. The overall size of the proposed antenna is 1.2λ × 0.8λ. The radiation patterns are roughly stable over the operating bandwidth with nearly endfire characteristic.

articleTitle: An improved broadband circularly polarized CPW fed slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An improved design of a broadband circularly polarized slot antenna fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) is proposed. Simulations indicate that the antenna obtains a 3-dB axial-ratio fractional bandwidth of 12.2% and a fractional 10-dB return-loss bandwidth of 60.3%, relative to the operating frequency of 1.65 GHz.

articleTitle: Underwater radiation fields of magnetic dipole array with 3×3 elements
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to further detect underwater targets, such as oil, gas, and shipboard equipment and so on, we discuss the underwater radiation fields of a magnetic dipole array with 3×3 elements in the TSS-FDTD method. Numerical results show that the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> and E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> amplitude and phase snapshots are symmetrical related to the z axis in the yoz plane in the working frequency f=180Hz. By analyzing the radiated fields, it is more readily to distinguish if there is an abnormal underwater target or not.

articleTitle: dA compact dual-band tunable filter adopting cross coupling structure
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact dual-band tunable bandpass filter operating in the range of 330MHz to 400MHz was proposed in this letter. The dual-band tunable bandpass filter was consisted of four rectangular ring tunable resonators and a cross type coupling structure. The cross type coupling structure also played the roles of a resonator. The desired performance of a dual-band tunable filter can be designed easily using the cross type coupling structure. The performance of the two passband can be adjusted dependently and has little influence to each other. The size of this tunable filter was less than 0.16λ*0.14λ normalized to 400MHz.

articleTitle: The nested complex source beam method with singular value decomposition
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work present a new aggregation procedure to improve the efficiency of the Nested Complex Source Beam (NCSB) method. The procedure is based on the application of the singular value decomposition (SVD) to the complex source beams (CSBs) aggregation matrices. The matrices, which represent the CSBs relationship between two adjacent levels, are decomposed into new combinations of the original CSBs. By choosing the most relevant singular values and singular vectors, a much more compact representation is obtained to accurately calculate the CSBs interactions. The numerical example is demonstrated to validate the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Doppler effect of wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The investigation into the effect of the wind turbines (WTs) on the radar system is increasing with the growing demands for wind farms. In order to evaluate the Doppler spectrum features of the rotational WT, a simplified WT model with high reliability is proposed and the simulation results are conducted in this paper. Then the Doppler effect under different characteristics are also analyzed by utilizing quasi-stationary method as well as the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).

articleTitle: Optimal design of LTCC filter by extracting human experience using fuzzy algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The fuzzy algorithm is applied to the optimization design of LTCC filter in order to achieve the ability of rapid design and automatic design. This method can be used to represent the expert information and numerical information in the form of if-then rule set. The fuzzy inference system is established to simulate the human thinking, which is used to design LTCC filter. Especially, when there are many the design parameters and the influence of the parameters on the filter is complex, this method can be effective in the design of LTCC filter. In order to verify the correctness of the proposed method, a LTCC filter is designed by using this method. The optimal results are compared with the measured results. It verifies the effectiveness and correctness of the fuzzy algorithm for the design of LTCC filters.

articleTitle: Discussion on the application of integrated RF system in the new armored platform
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to meet the higher requirements of the future information warfare on the electronic RF system of tank armored platform, this paper presents that the integrated RF system should be applied to the new armored platform. The system is designed with the method of synthetic aperture; it can complete the functions such as airborne target search, precise tracking, threat assessment, electronic warfare, damage assessment. The system plays a very important role in the protection of armored platform. Firstly, the multifunction integrated RF system of armored platform is introduced. Secondly, the composition, function and characteristics of the system are analyzed in detail, and the application mode of the system is briefly described. Finally, the development suggestions are put forward for the further application of the integrated RF system in the new tank and armored platform.

articleTitle: The study of the rough medium surface by improved IPO
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Iterative physical optics (IPO) is one of the important methods in the study of electromagnetic scattering. In this paper, the formula of IPO based on PO is derived. Based on the formula, the bistatic scattering and back scattering of dielectric sea surface with different incident angles are calculated, and the calculation results are compared with the FEKO built-in numerical algorithm for multilayer fast multipole (MLFMM) method and physical optics (PO). In order to improve the operation efficiency, a kind of the CPU parallel acceleration, OpenMP technology, is introduced, which effectively reduces the time consumption of the iterative process.

articleTitle: Imaging simulation based on fully polarimetric radar of simple manmade targets in a half space
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper is based on the application requirements of fully polarimetric radar for near ground and sea targets detection. We have used numerical modeling based on integral equation and multilevel fast multipole algorithm to study and calculate the fully polarimetric far field scattering data of simple manmade targets in a half space to conduct radar imaging. We also have compared the differences of electromagnetic scattering characteristics of some manmade targets with different heights above ground or sea and the radar images. The results have been presented to demonstrated that the combination of the electromagnetic numerical modeling and the radar imaging could identify the simple targets in a half space. The proposed methods could be used to simulate a set of polarimetric radar system to detect manmade targets near ground and sea.

articleTitle: Wideband and miniature conical helix antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A miniature and wideband helix antenna with gradient radius is proposed in this paper. The contour of the antenna is as a cone with small bottom and large top radius. An extra microstrip line is connected to the bottom end of the helix for impedance matching. The antenna is modeled and simulated. The simulated results show that the antenna can cover the bandwidth of 40% in X-band. It's expected this antenna can be a candidate of antenna design with limited size, wide bandwidth, circular polarization and simple structure properties.

articleTitle: A triple-band substrate integrated waveguide antenna based on metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a triple-band substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) antenna is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a T-shaped radiator, where it is etched on the top side of the common dielectric substrate and fed by a substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) feed-line. Embedded in the E-plane of the antenna are two arrays of zero-index matamaterials (ZIM) unit-cells whose purpose is to effectively confine the electromagnetic waves in the end-fire direction to achieve triple-band characteristics. By properly optimizing the antenna dimensions, the impedance bandwidth(S11<;-10 dB) is 3.08 GHz (23.09-26.17 GHz), 3.49 GHz (27.62-31.11 GHz) and 2.20 GHz (31.81-34.47 GHz) around 24 GHz, 29 GHz and 33 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A multi-order radiative transfer model for microwave radiometry of vegetation canopies
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Quantitative understanding of the relationship between scattering mechanisms within vegetation canopies and the microwave brightness temperature is desirable for soil moisture retrievals over vegetated landscapes. In this study, a multi-order radiative transfer model is developed to more accurately account for vegetation canopy scattering by modifying the basic τ-ω model. The multi-order solution is used to investigate this relationship and to perform a physical analysis of the scattered and emitted radiation from vegetation canopies. The model is tested against Multi-frequency Microwave Radiometer brightness temperature measurements acquired over deciduous soybean and cotton by a truck-mounted microwave instrument system called TMMR in 2009. The model predictions are in good agreement with the data, and they give quantitative understanding for the influence of multi-order scattering within the canopy on the brightness temperature. The results show that the scattering term is significant for the vegetation canopies and modifications are necessary to the τ-ω model when applied to dense vegetation.

articleTitle: Optical and electrical properties of short-pitch plasmonic solar cells with oblique incidence
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The optical and electrical properties of organic solar cells (OSCs) with short-pitch metallic gratings introduced in conventional OSCs are investigated in the case of oblique incidence. Finite-difference frequency-domain (FDFD) method is applied to solve the Maxwell's equations and semiconductor equations for obtaining the optical and electrical properties of OSCs. It is found the light absorption is greatly enhanced due to surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is excited by introducing short-pitch gratings. Meanwhile, short-circuit current and power conversion efficiency have been increased accordingly. With the increase of incident angle, the light absorption decreases instead. Since the absorption decreases with the increase of incident angle, the electrical properties (short-circuit current and power conversion efficiency) obviously have been reduced. These results contribute to better understanding both optical and electrical properties of OSCs.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized omnidirectional antennas with folded structures
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we have presented two designs of dual-polarized antennas with omnidirectional radiation patterns in the azimuthal plane. For the first design, the vertical polarization is provided by a monopole with a co-planar waveguide feed; and the horizontal polarization is provided by a slot-coupled folded dipole structure. In order to reduce the antenna dimensions, the second design uses another method to achieve horizontal polarization with omnidirectional pattern. A slot-coupled cavity is utilized and integrated with the monopole, which is also used for vertical polarization. For both designs, the simulated bandwidths cover the desired band of 2.4-2.48 GHz with S11(S22)<;-10 dB and S21<;-20 dB. The gain variation is smaller than 3 dB for both polarizations. What's more, for the second design, the antenna has a compact volume of 52×29×9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (0.42λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.24λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.07λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 2.44 GHz).

articleTitle: A study of multipath scattering from low-altitude target above complex ocean surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper aims at simulating the multipath effect of EM scattering from low altitude target above large scale complex ocean surface. The complexity is reflected by the composite description of both large scale profile and small roughness structures of the ocean surface model. The scattering from ocean surface is calculated by a Modified Facet-based Two Scale Model. The model decomposed ocean surface into a mount of large and slightly rough facets with foam layer superimposed as the microscopic roughness. Specular and diffuse scattering from long and short waves are both involved by KA and SPM. The volume scattering from the foam layer is considered by Vector Radiative Transfer (VRT) theory. Simulations can agree well with the measurement results. Finally, Multipath scattering between target and ocean surface are invovled by an extended image theory.

articleTitle: Compact power divider based on composite right/left-handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A miniaturized power divider based on composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) is proposed in this paper. The simulated results show that the each output port of the power divider is able to achieve equal-amplitude and in-phase electromagnetic (EM) signal in the frequency range from 2.35GHz to 2.42GHz. The measured results is good agreement with the simulated one. The proposed power divider is very compact which can be acted as feeding network of miniaturized microstrip antenna array.

articleTitle: A quick measurement method of the terminal equivalent impedance for multiple parallel cable-bundles
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, based on electromagnetic theory and multi-conductor transmission lines(MTL) theory, proposes a quick measurement method of the terminal equivalent impedance for multiple parallel cable-bundles. According to the method, the multiple cable-bundles are treated as equivalent of MTL firstly. After that, using vector network analyzer(VNA) and current probe measures broadband voltage reflection coefficients at two locations of each cable-bundle. Then construct nonlinear equations about terminal equivalent resistances, at last solve the equations and acquire broadband terminal equivalent resistance for each cable-bundle.

articleTitle: The design of a five-band antenna based on coplanar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel multiple-band antenna, fed by the coplanar waveguide(CPW), is proposed in this paper. The design is based on an ultra-wideband(UWB) antenna. By using PIN diodes, the structure of the antenna could be changeable, which means the operating frequency could be reconfigurable. After optimizing the parameters, the antenna can resonant among the following five bands 1920~2170MHz(UMTS), 2300~2400MHz(LTE2300), 2400~2484MHz(Bluetooth), 3400~3690MHz(WIMAX), 5150 ~5350MHz(WLAN), and in each state the antenna has good omnidirectional radiating characteristics.

articleTitle: Impact of excitation coefficients orthogonalization on beam forming
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The beam-forming principle of multiple feeds per beam is highly concerned in multiple spot beam antennas of communication satellites because of its reflectors reduction. However, the isolation between the adjacent beams is decreased and the complexity of the networks is increased if some feeds of the adjacent clusters are shared. A valid way of keeping the excitations of adjacent beams orthogonal is introduced to cope with these issues. This paper introduces the theory of excitation coefficients orthogonalization and its essential conditions. Along with the method of excitations optimization is presented. Then the optimized result is compared with a feed per beam and classical seven feeds per beam in performance, especially in the main indexes of triple beam crossover level and carrier to interference ratio (C/I). The result indicates that the beam under orthogonality constraints is more balanced in the main properties.

articleTitle: The comparison of scattering from model on the Lake to target on the sea based on FSV
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Feature Selective Validation (FSV) Method has been developed as a standard method to mimic an expert's opinion of concurrence between simulation and measurement datasets. This paper presents a comparison of Scattering from model on the Lake to Target on the Sea. Based on the NRCS curves these datasets should appear trendly and quantitive similar. The objective is to present a basic evaluation of the FSV method for the scattering from complex targets. The spectra of wind waves in lake Michigan was introduced for computing the electromagnetic scattering from the rough lake surface. In addition, the JONSWAP ocean spectrum is used in this article to generate numerical data for the scattering of random rough sea surface.

articleTitle: Non-data-aided timing recovery scheme for MSK signals
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the signal decomposition expression for Minimum Shift Keying (MSK) signals. The Phase of MSK signal with real parts and imaginary parts is recovered from discrete-Fourier-transform of signal appropriate parts, and then Phase is translated into time. Based on this, a non-data-aided timing recovery is proposed for MSK signals by absolute algorithm. Compared with the existing algorithm, the proposed scheme is more superior in performance and is close to Modified Cramer-Rao Bound (MCRB).

articleTitle: Design of multistage gradient coaxial based on axial dislocation compensation method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Impedance matching is the essential requirement in the design of a coaxial structure. The abrupt change of the inner and outer diameter of the coaxial structure will lead to the change of its characteristic impedance, and then enormous reflection would be excited if the failure of the proper design. In this article, a structure of multistage gradient coaxial is built, which is based on the axial dislocation compensation method (ADCM). Then, its performance is investigated through CST simulation and the theory of equivalent two port network. The contrastive results show that the VSWR of the presented structure through ADCM with equivalent circuit method much better than empirical method in the entire wave range of investigated. In addition, the combination of multistage buffering gradient method and ADCM can be used to suppress the reflection for the large scale gradient coaxial structure.

articleTitle: Scattering of a uniaxial anisotropic sphere incident by a Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beam
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The analytical theory for the scattering of a uniaxial anisotropic illuminated by a Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beam is presented. Based on the complex source point method and the relation between Hermite polynomial and Laguerre polynomial, the expansion of Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beam expanded in terms of spherical vector wave functions is derived. Using the continuous boundary condition at the surface of the sphere, the scattering coefficients are obtained. The scattering intensity distributions of a uniaxial anisotropic sphere incident by a Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beam are numerically analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: An improved design of ortho-mode transducer
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An Ortho-mode Transducer(OMT) used for Dual-beam and dual-polarization reflector antenna is proposed for the problem of large lateral offset-focus. The matching of the transducer is analyzed by analyzing the electronic properties of the waveguide. The experimental results are in good agreement with the numerical simulations. Compared to the traditional OMT used screws outside the waveguide, this new structure can realize the minimum space between the two feed systems.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband bow-ties for hidden target detection
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) through-wall radar is not able to meet the requirement of high resolution to detect hidden objects in some circumstance. This paper proposes an ultra broadband dual polarization radar antenna unit. The principles of the improved conical antenna is employed to make the antenna structure contour transit smoothly, the reflection coefficient of current is small. Thus, the impedance bandwidth of the antenna can be extended effectively. Additionally, a 1:2 balanced to unbalanced transmission line transformer is adopted. Simulation and experimental results show that the dual polarization antenna achieves unidirectional radiation and a relative bandwidth of 101%. The proposed antenna can achieve high gain and without loading any extra structure.

articleTitle: Observations on the irregularities using Kunming VHF radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using the data from Kunming(103.7°E, 25.6°N) VHF coherent radar, Low-latitude ionospheric E-region irregularities of primrose season are investigated. The observational results shows that E-region irregularities occur mostly at nighttime, mainly appears in the night, especially in the midnight of LT, the height ranges extensively from 110 to 160km.

articleTitle: An analysis of Doppler frequency shift in 2D modificated space plasma
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To study the Doppler shift phenomenon in the propagation of the short-wave signal in the ionosphere with heated F layer, the ionosphere is divided into two kinds of different parts of the normal ionosphere and the heating ionosphere. Then the expression of Doppler shift can be derived through the two part's motion. In the case of ignoring the influence of electron density with time and geomagnetic field, Numerical simulation of expression of Doppler shift in artificial heating region is presented. In the light of simulation results, the influence of different factors on Doppler shift is analyzed.

articleTitle: Study on the time domain electromagnetic sputtering effect of the slot array with dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In some applications, the amplitude of the time domain scattering field waveform of object might be very large at the beginning, and becomes smaller only when the interaction reaches stable state. This phenomenon is defined as the time domain electromagnetic sputtering effect. In this paper, the sputtering effect is studied for possible use in detecting the low radar cross section (RCS) objects. It is analyzed using the time domain reflection coefficient and Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) simulation. Different parameters of dielectric substrate are considered in the analysis of the time duration of the sputtering effects.

articleTitle: A modeling approach for complex multifloored indoor environments
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The prediction accuracy of an indoor ray tracing model is obviously affected by the accuracy of environment information. Thus, a modeling approach for the choice of the environment information is presented in this paper. To provide good prediction accuracy using an indoor ray tracing model, the present study divides the indoor environment modeling in two ways: geometric modeling and electrical parameter modeling. The former affects the determination of propagation paths, while the latter affects electromagnetic field calculations of propagation paths arriving at receiver. This indoor environment modeling is to assist in selecting the appropriate level of accuracy required in indoor databases to achieve good trade-offs between database costs and prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Exploration and practice on the course of "analysis of electronic information business case"
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we establish an inquiry learning curriculum model under a cooperative environment by inducting business case analysis method to electronic information engineering courses. Smart phones, mobile communication, internet, EPC system network are treated as objects to be explored. We discuss the reason of becoming "hot" industry and the aspects including product design, cost control, marketing, business models, technology standards, entrepreneurship and innovation. The contents, operation, evaluation on the course of "Analysis of Electronic Information Business Case (AEIBC)" are introduced in this paper. The evaluation results indicate that the course of AEIBC helps to broaden students' horizons, stimulate enthusiasm for learning, improve teamwork and communication skills, and establish the initial awareness of entrepreneurship, cost, patent, standard, network.

articleTitle: A multi-band planar printed antenna for WLAN/WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new multi-band planar printed antenna was designed for frequency bands of WLAn and WiMAX. By adding a smaller coupling circle ring and a single branch on the bigger circle ring, three resonant frequencies were generated. The measured results show that the return losses at band of 2.5/3.5/5.3 GHz (WLAN/WiMAX) are all less than -10dB. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Rectangular grating surface plasmon interference model equivalent numerical experiment
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the Equivalent Current Theory of optical waveguide coupling, the electric field distribution of grating structure and notch groove slit are derived. Beam divergence angle with different grating notch groove and light intensity of non-uniform array antenna structure are numerical simulated. Beam light field background comparison diagram with different notch groove current amplitude and the influence of phase difference on beam peak position are shown. The results show that with the number of grating notch groove becomes larger, beam divergence angle becomes smaller and amplitude larger and beam light fields background darker. In addition, the larger current the grating notch groove is, the darker the background light fields are. With the phase difference increases, the main peak position moves to right. The conclusions above provide theoretical basis for the beam direction modulation and control.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of S-band radar sea cluttter spikes
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the S-band sea clutter data measured by the radar located on a cliff top employed, this work compares the amplitude characteristics of the sea clutter in S-band and X-band (IPIX data). On this basis, the difference of the sea spike properties between the two radar bands is analyzed both in time and frequency domain. The identification method of the sea spike from the sea clutter background uses the spike amplitude, the minimum spike width and the minimum interval between spikes, as three qualitative parameters. Comparing with X-band, the specificity of the sea spikes in S-band is presented.

articleTitle: Investigation of material parameters and SAR distribution in human tissue using FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper firstly introduces elementary knowledge of bio-electromagnetic dose, and then elaborates on the method and steps of theoretical bio-electromagnetic dose used to compute the electromagnetic dose absorbed by human body at the frequency 300MHz and 3GHz. Afterwards, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is utilized to analyze the dielectric property and calculate the specific absorption rate (SAR) in several biological organizations of human body and the results produced from this calculating process are compared with proven conclusions. The method and implementation steps used in this article suits for computing dielectric property of multi-layered biological tissue under the irradiation of arbitrary frequency electromagnetic wave. Therefore, the analysis method can lay quantitative foundation of research on the bio-effects of electromagnetic waves, on the mechanism of the bio-effect, on application of the bio-effects, and on the formulation for safety standard of electromagnetic wave radiation.

articleTitle: Some acceleration techniques for antenna simulation in FDTD
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Optimization of array operation and the internal expressions of loops for serial finite-difference time-domain(FDTD) codes in C language is presented in this paper. Then the Parallelized FDTD on MPI platform and OpenMP is introduced. Some examples of antenna simulation are given. The results show that computing time is saved as those acceleration techniques used in serial/parallelized FDTD codes, the results from Parallelized FDTD on MPI and OpenMP are same with those only on MPI, and both of them are agreed well with those of software.

articleTitle: An optimized interference alignment algorithm based on dynamic power allocation for MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: High density small cells with large number of simultaneously connected devices will be controlled by the macro cell in the future 5G wireless standards. In this context, interference management becomes critical in achieving high spectral efficiency. An approach called interference alignment (IA) technique has shown great promise in many theoretical studies. However, the performance improvement brought by IA in the MIMO interference network has not been investigated well when combined with power allocation. In this paper, we propose a joint IA and power allocation algorithm that designed to find the interference mitigation solution and allocate power among different data streams of the users with less computational cost. The proposed algorithm combines the maximum of total system signal interference noise ratio (Max-SINR) criterion and the maximum chord distance of channel matrix criterion not only maximize the distances between the interference subspace and the signal spanned, but also further reduce the interference between users by power allocation. Further, the algorithm in this paper which does not use iterative to get the precoding matrix or the mitigation matrix minimizes the complexity of the whole system and has better engineering applicability. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms other known interference alignment algorithms in terms of throughput and the energy efficiency, which also accord with the green communications.

publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: antennas; EM theory; computational electromagnetics; electromagnetic compatibility; and propagation.

articleTitle: A study of defect modes in one dimensional electromagnetic band gap structures
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structures have great potential in microwave communications. This paper reports a study of defect modes in one dimensional EBG structures. Effects of the size and permittivity of a defect in one dimensional EBG structure on the band gap property were investigated. Samples of EBG structures were fabricated by a cutting and inserting method. Transmission properties of these EBGs were simulated using a high frequency structure simulator and measured through a transmission/refection method. The defect mode was analyzed based on interference theory of electromagnetic waves and the resonance frequencies were calculated accordingly. The calculated results are in good accordance with the simulation and measurement. This research extends the study on the physical features of defects in EBG structures, providing a way to tune the working frequencies of EBG-type wireless communication devices.

articleTitle: Single-layer differential CPW-fed UWB antenna with common-mode suppressed and band notched applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A single-layer differential coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed antenna is proposed for common-mode suppressed and WLAN band notched ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The UWB nature is generated by the stepped slot radiators and a pair of differential stepped CPW feeding lines. When two ports of the antenna are fed with common-mode signals, the radiator cannot be excited and common-mode suppression is obtained. Moreover, a pair of U-shaped slits and stubs are etched on the CPW lines and stepped slots to earn a notch band characteristic. Then, to validate the presented antenna, a prototype antenna is fabricated and tested. The proposed antenna shows experimentally differential reflection coefficients -10 dB bandwidth of 122.6% (2.54-10.6 GHz). A measured band notch at 5.1-5.9 GHz for WLAN band is also obtained. Moreover, the common-mode suppression within the operating band better than 1.5 dB is achieved. All the results shows that the proposed antenna can be widely used in UWB wireless communication systems, medical imaging systems and vehicular radars.

articleTitle: Application perspective of Qujing incoherent scatter radar acting as a high power source at 500MHz
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Incoherent Scatter Radar is the most powerful tool to measure the ionosphere on the ground. Its high power output provides us a unique opportunity in some research fields more than the ionosphere sounding. The potential application perspective of the QJISR (25.6°N, 103.8°E), the first one in China, acting as the high power source is described including the bi- or multi-static receiving of signal scattered from the troposphere, ionosphere, space debris, meteoroid etc.

articleTitle: An improved type of TEn mode circular polarizer
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An improved type of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode circular polarizer consisting of a rectangular dielectric membrane and a ladder-shaped dielectric transition is proposed. The rectangular membrane is placed at 0=44.9° relative to the axial direction of a circular waveguide rather than 45° theoretically in order to realize a circular polarization, and the transition acts as a impedance-matching role for the purpose of reducing the wave reflection. Simulation is done to verify the performances of the design and shows that two electric components of the output port are nearly equal and the phase difference between them is 90° ± 3.50° in the frequency range from 29.5 to 30.5 GHz. Furthermore, Axial rati-o(AR) <; 0.48dB and VSWR<; 1.12 in the whole bandwidth.

articleTitle: Radar echo simulation using wideband sweep frequency data
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The aim of this article is to study a technique of simulating the Radar echo for high-speed dynamic target. Firstly, swept wideband echo model under static measurement and LFM echo model under dynamic measurement were established based on diverse signals transmitted in static measurement and dynamic measurement. The method for simulating the LFM echo of high-speed dynamic targets after "dechirp" using static measured data was studied based on the detailed analysis about the difference between the above two signal models. The applicability of the proposed technique was analyzed in the simulation experiment.

articleTitle: A multi-mode and multi-frequency handset antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A multi-mode and multi-frequency handset antenna is proposed for navigation and communication handset system in this paper. The antenna consists of monopole, dipole and quadrifilar helix which are integrated co-axially, operating on UHF(400-470MHz), WLAN(2.4GHz) and GPS(1575.42MHz). The antenna shows good performances, such as VSWR is less that 2 for all bands, 0 dBi, 2 dBi and 2.5dBi antenna gain on UHF, WLAN and GPS bands respectively. The antenna used for UHF and WLAN is linear polarization, while the antenna used for GPS is right-hand circular polarization. And isolation between them is less than -30 dB.

articleTitle: Research on reducing grating lobe of adjoining regular subarray using genetic algorithms (GA)
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of grating lobe caused by large array element spacing in adjoining regular subarray, a method based on genetic algorithms applications (GA), which can reduce grating lobe of adjoining regular subarray, has been proposed. Firstly, considering the demands of antenna aperture, the design determined appropriate number of subarrays. Then, with the purpose of reducing grating lobe of adjoining regular subarray, the design optimized the layout of the adjoining regular subarray, which could be used to break the periodicity of subarray layout. The writing procedure of GA code is based on the Matlab software, and in order to verify the reliability of simulation results obtained from Matlab software, HFSS (based on finite element technique) was used. Under the circumstance of same amplitude and phase, simulation results show that largest grating lobe has been reduced 3dBi with the irregular subarray layout, which proves the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed program.

articleTitle: Parallel FDTD method for EM scattering from a rough surface with a target
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The finite-difference time domain (FDTD), a numerical method, is an accurate approach to calculate the electromagnetic scattering coefficients of target and rough surface. However, it is very time-consuming to solve the problem for FDTD executing on a single CPU. We develop the CUDA-based parallel FDTD to accelerate the computation of electromagnetic scattering from a three-dimensional target and a two-dimensional rough surface. The FDTD lattices are truncated by a uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML), and finite difference equations are employed in the whole computation domain. Our optimization efforts on GPU-accelerated FDTD for a target and a rough surface model can be achieved at a speedup of 40.16× on NVIDIA Tesla K40c GPU.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of field uniformity of reverberation chamber
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper builds a three-dimension electromagnetic model of a reverberation chamber and solves the electromagnetic field distribution through finite element method. This paper deals with data of electromagnetic field through statistics, and attains statistical parameters such as correlation coefficient and standard deviation. To validate the simulation results, this paper compares the simulation results and the measurement data including electromagnetic field distribution and statistical parameters of field uniformity. The comparison shows that both is consistent with each other, and precision of simulation is good.

articleTitle: Bidirectional reflection distribution function modeling of material surface in different temperature
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the Planck's law and integrality the directional hemisphere reflectivity (DHR) and the Kirchhoffs law. And referred to the Torrance-Sparrow model and the five-parameter semi-empirical model, a new Bidirectional reflection distribution function model (BRDF) is developed in different temperature of material surface, this model will be applicable for various materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of RCS of certain rough targets in terahertz band
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: RCS of a waving target with uniform rough distribution is calculated by Physical Optics (PO) Method in Ka and Terahertz Bands respectively. So is another assembly consisting of a cylinder and a little cubic. The results show that the RCS of the two targets are different both in amplitude and symmetry. For a certain target, the results demonstrate that EM wave in terahertz band has a higher resolution compared with that of Ka band.

articleTitle: Capacitor-loaded circularly polarized annular-ring slotted microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper studies a simple and novel annular-ring slotted microstrip patch antenna loaded by a surface mount chip capacitor for circularly polarized (CP) radiation. By connecting the capacitor with a proper value across the annular-ring slot at an appropriate position, the fundamental resonant mode of the microstrip patch antenna can be degenerated into two orthogonal modes with equal amplitude and quadrature phase. Hence, CP radiation can be obtained. An antenna prototype was fabricated and measured. The simulation and measurement results validate that the proposed antenna has excellent CP characteristics at the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Study on the transmission characteristics of a double layered complementary frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new double layered complementary frequency selective surface (FSS) based on square ring is proposed. One side of the FSS is an improved type of square ring metal patch, and the other side is a complementary metal screen. The transmission characteristics of the proposed FSS are studied. Meanwhile, the incident wave with different incident angles or with different polarization modes are analyzed respectively. Numerical simulation and actual measurements have shown that the new frequency selective surface has improved stability for different incident directions and polarizations, and it will provide a valuable reference for the design of FSS complementary screen.

Author Keywords: double layer complementary frequency selective surface

articleTitle: A method separating echo by adaptive chirplet signal decomposition based on FRFT
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The movement of actual target is non-stationary, usually accompanied by rotation, swing and other non-rigid motion in the process of high speed flight. Adaptive joint time-frequency analysis is available to estimate target's motion characteristics. To solve the problem of complex of parameter estimation in the time-frequency signal decomposition, a method using adaptive chirplet signal decomposition based on fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is proposed. First perform the estimated signal with consecutive FRFT, and search for local maximum. The fractional Fourier transform order number which corresponding the maximum is converted into the angle. Repeat this step, and calculating every energy focus point respectively in fractional Fourier domain, finally the adaptive chirplet signal decomposition is completed based on Chirp signal detection and parameter estimation in fractional Fourier domain. This method estimates a fewer number of parameters in signal decomposition, and has good noise immunity. The analysis of simulation proves the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Wideband loop antenna based on composite right/left-handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband loop antenna based on four unit cells of composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) is proposed in this paper. The unit cell is composed of a ladder network with two series capacitors and shunt inductors. The loop antenna based on four-cell nonperiodic CRLH-TL shows wider bandwidth performance when comparing with the periodically loaded loop antenna with the same size. The measured results are good agreement with the simulated ones. The proposed loop antenna is implemented in plane technology which is very compact and can be acted as commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of abnormal incoherent scatter spectra based on Zakharov model
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: When high power electromagnetic waves with frequencies near the peak plasma frequency are transmitted into the ionosphere, the parametric decay instability will be stimulated around the reflection altitude, which will excite Langmuir turbulence and enhance incoherent scatter spectra later. According to typical parameters of ionospheric modify-cation facilities at Tromse, the incoherent scatter spectra at F region altitudes are simulated based on Zakharov model. With parameters changed, the effects of effective radiated power and heating frequency on spectra are discussed and the characteristics of spectra are analyzed. It turns out that the right shoulder of the ion lines at lower altitudes is enhanced significantly while the left shoulder is increased markedly at higher altitudes and the parametric decay instability is verified to be stimulated in simulation.

articleTitle: An improved DOA estimation algorithm based on sparse reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
