abstract: The use of sparse reconstruction for DOA estimation has the advantages of low requirement for the number of snapshots and applicative for coherent signal etc. The solution of sparse signals is generally translated into the L0 norm minimization problem. This paper proposes a new threshold function to approximate L0 norm optimization combined with Newton method, besides, it further puts forward the improved algorithm which using singular value decomposition method to improve the stability of the algorithm. Simulation results show that under the same test conditions, the algorithm in this paper compared with the MUSIC algorithm, SL0 algorithm and OMP algorithm in the reconstruction accuracy and peak signal to noise ratio is greatly improved, also in the low signal-to-noise ratio and low sampling snapshot condition, can obtain good estimation performance.

articleTitle: Estimation of multipath parameters in wireless communications using noncircular PARAFAC algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a noncircular PARAFAC (NC-PARAFAC)-based algorithm is developed for joint angle and delay estimation (JADE) in a multipath communication scenario. To utilize the inherent multidimensional structure in the received data, a three-order tensor is formulated which linked the estimations of angle and delay to the PARAFAC model. To further exploit the property of noncircular signals, an expanded PARAFAC decomposition algorithm is presented. The proposed algorithm doubles the array aperture, thus it has better JADE accuracy than the existing methods. The proposed algorithm does not require spectral peak searching or eigenvalue decomposition of the received signal covariance matrix, and it can achieve automatic pairing of the estimated parameters. Extensive numerical experiments verify the effectiveness and improvement of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Fast design of multilayer cascade metasurface absorbers using particle swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A fast design procedure of multilayer cascade metasurface absorbers is presented. By analyzing the equivalent circuit model and applying the circuit parameter extraction method, a rapid design procedure can be realized. Combined with the particle swarm optimization, an optimized performance and structure parameters of the multilayer cascade metasurface absorber can be obtained. Compared with the conventional design methods, the proposed design procedure has the advantages of fast calculation speed and small memory consumption. By applying the proposed design procedure, a three-layer metasurface absorber with outstanding performances is realized. The absorption coefficient of the absorber reaches 90% in a broadband from 2.0GHz to 17.5GHz. The full-wave simulation result agrees well with the result obtained from the equivalent circuit model which verifies the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed design procedure.

articleTitle: Dual-band conformal meander-line monopole antenna with coupled patch for unmanned aerial vehicle applications
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a meander-line monopole antenna for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UVA). In order to improve the resonant characteristic and expand the bandwidth, a couple of coupled patches have been added. It also improves the radiation characteristics in higher frequency. The antenna realizes omni-directional radiation in the horizontal plane when operating in780MHz-900MHz and 1.20GHz-2.28GHz. The antenna is conformed on the side of airframe and can be widely used as communication antenna on UVAs for its performance of dual-band and wideband.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiment study of horn antenna loaded with ENZ metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The design of horn antenna loaded with a quasi-period structure is presented in this paper, to achieve higher aperture efficiency. The novel structure is composed of a double-layer metallic holes array. Simulation and experiments show that new design can get more uniform phase distribution than the normal horn without ENZ layer, the gain is enhanced 3dB, and the aperture efficiency is increased from 0.5 to above 0.9.

articleTitle: A novel wearable 3D printed RFID badge tag
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel 3D RFID badge tag fabricated by 3D printing technology is proposed. The badge shape facilitates the tag's integration with clothes for the purposes of identification and access control. The proposed tag features a compact size (radius 20 mm, height 5 mm) and a good performance with a simulated maximum reading range of 9.7 m (4.0 W EIRP) in the RFID FCC band (902-928 MHz). Furthermore, the 3D printing technology dramatically reduces the fabrication time and cost.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-band dual-polarized slot antenna for Ku-band video satellite application
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized slot antenna for Ku-band video satellite application is proposed. It mainly consists of the ground with a wide slot and a reflector. The orthogonal modes are excited by slot-coupling feeding and microstrip feeding to realize dual polarization. The dual-band characteristic is realized using the multi-resonant performance of wide slot. The impedance bandwidth for two port covers the dual wide bandwidths of 10.7-11.7GHz and 11.7-12.7GHz. The gain can be up to 8.8dBi. The proposed antenna has low profile, simple structure, good port isolation and high gain. It is a good candidate for Ku-band video satellite antenna.

articleTitle: Studying the effects of the rough sea surface on electromagnetic waves propagation
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic waves (EWs) propagation on the rough sea surface simulated by the parabolic equation (PE) method is presented in this paper. The sea surface is simulated by the Elfouhaily spectrum and Longuet-Higgins model. In this sea surface propagation model, the relations between the effects of the rough sea surface on the EWs propagation and the wind speed, wind direction and the frequency of the EWs are studied. The simulation results of the rough sea surface model are compared with those of the Miller-Brown model. It demonstrates that, in a certain extent, the influence of the rough sea surface on the EWs propagation increases with the wind speed and the angle between the wind direction and the propagation direction, and decreases with the frequency of the EWs.

articleTitle: Fast solution of linear systems with many right hand sides using MPI parallel interpolative decomposition
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The interpolative decomposition (ID) has been employed to find the skeleton excitations for the applications where many incidents have to be repeatedly solved. The algorithm is accuracy controllable and efficient. However, the peak memory usage may be the bottleneck of the decomposition when the number of unknowns and that of incidents become large. In this work, the parallel ID is developed to alleviate the difficulty. Numerical experiments have been conducted to demonstrate the performance of the proposed parallel scheme.

articleTitle: Dual band directional bowtie antenna loaded with a square loop
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study presents a newly modified unidirectional bowtie antenna with dual-band operation. The proposed antenna consists of two bowtie dipole elements, a square loop, a parallel-strip line (changed from a microstrip line), and a ground plane. The dual-wideband operating characteristics of this antenna are achieved by means of the square loop. Experimental results show that the proposed antenna has wide dual-band impedance bandwidths ranging from 2.64 to 6.28 GHz and from 8 to 14 GHz, respectively. Moreover, desirable directional radiation patterns showing gains of greater than 6.5 dBi for 2.64-6.28 GHz (81.6%) and 9.35-12.7 GHz (30.4%) bands are achieved.

articleTitle: On configuration and working model of Massive MIMO antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Focusing on the design of the large number of antennas in massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO), this paper has proposed a configuration of the antennas for massive MIMO, and presented a possible working model based on the idea of dynamic combination of the multiple antennas and the antenna arrays. The upper limit of the number of antenna elements for beamforming in the massive MIMO system is studied. Then the zero-forcing (ZF) precoding and quaternary phase-shift keying (QPSK) modulation are applied to evaluate bit error rate (BER) of the proposed configuration. Finally, the simulation results have been given to show the performance of the configuration and the working model proposed in this paper.

Author Keywords: combination of antenna array and multiple antennas

articleTitle: Noncontact measurement of rotational movement using IR-UWB radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper addresses a noncontact measurement application of customized signal processing using the impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) radar to realize the rotational speed detection. Microwave radar technology offers a noncontact, quick, accurate technique and has potential for industrial applications. We studied the effect of suppression to remove the stationary background clutter, and separated the front rotor and the back one of electric fan from the overlapped echo signal using the power-spectrum density (PSD) analysis. The experimental results have shown the accuracy and robustness of our system to detect the speed of angular movement such as electric fans or other motor rotation. It has been shown that the frequency analysis will have a dominant fundamental frequency that is multiple of the rotation frequency that depends on the structure of reflectors on the target in IR-UWB radar based noncontact rotational movement measurement.

articleTitle: A slotted dielectric substrate loaded broadband Vivaldi antenna fed by SIW
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel compact slotted dielectric substrate loaded broadband Vivaldi antenna is proposed. This antenna consists of a typical antipodal SIW Vivaldi antenna and two pieces of FR4 substrate with uneven thickness and periodic slots, two pieces of FR4 substrate is symmetrically loaded on Vivaldi antenna above and under respectively. The effects of different thickness distribution and slots on substrate were simulated. Simulated results exhibit that the antenna achieves a gain of 10.1 ± 0.7 dBi over the frequency of 27-45GHz with reflection coefficient less than -14dB.

articleTitle: Radar cross section reduction of a microstrip antenna with CSRRs loaded on the ground
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the peculiar refractive index feature of complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR), a low-RCS (LR) microstrip antenna is proposed. By loading CSRRs on the ground plane along two adjacent edges of the radiation patch, the scattering field is deflected and a spatial reduction of out-band radar cross section (RCS) is achieved. Due to the polarization selective characteristics of CSRR, each CSRR will play its role in the RCS reduction with incident waves of corresponding polarization. Maximum RCS reduction values of 19.9 dBsm and 17.8 dBsm with x- and j-polarization incident waves are achieved respectively.

articleTitle: Propagation of electromagnetic waves in a glow-discharge dusty plasma
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic wave in a glow discharge plasma with dust particles are experimentally studied. A special discharge structure has successfully produced argon AC glow discharge plasma. Measurements of the plasma parameters using Langmuir probes, in the absence of the dust particles, give plasma densities n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> ~5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and electron temperatures ranging from Te=2 to 4 eV. Dusty plasmas are made by suspending 30 nm radius aluminum oxide (Al2O3) particles in the argon plasma. Dust in the device have densities n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The propagation characteristics of electromagnetic wave are determined by vector network analyzer with antennas in 4-6 GHz. An apparent attenuation by the dust is observed, and the measured attenuation data are approximately in accordance with the curve of theory calculation. The results show that the charged dust particles play a significant role of the microwave attenuation. The effects of gas pressure and input power is investigated in the dusty plasma. The results show that the transmission attenuation increase with the increasing gas pressure and input power.

articleTitle: Analysis and control of shielding effectiveness for a rectangular enclosure with a rectangular aperture
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic environment has become more complex due to the rapid development of modern electronic techniques, and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problems caused by outside interference have become a big issue for many devices, and cannot be ignored. To minimize the impact from outer electromagnetic interference, metallic enclosure is widely used as a shield. Therefore, shielding effectiveness (SE) of enclosure becomes a critical factor that affects EMC of equipment. In this paper, a rectangular enclosure with a rectangular aperture is studied, and an equivalent circuit model for SE evaluation is built via a vector fitting (VF) tool. The equivalent circuit saves time and calculating resource during simulation, and can be used to predict the SE performance efficiently. Also, equivalent circuit offers a new angle of view for better SE comprehension, and is applied to control SE of the rectangular enclosure.

articleTitle: A handover scheme for seamless multicasting in PMIPv6 wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: PMIPv6 is a mobile-controlled mobility management protocol. If the MN performs handover in the PMIPv6 network, the MAG performs handover procedure with LMA directly on behalf of the MN. By the means of proxy, the MN doesn't need to perform handover procedure. And thus many signal messages can be reduced between MAG and MN. As a Moblie Node moves through the wireless network environment, the events of handover are inevitable. Binding delay and packet loss during the handover process severely weaken the wireless service quality, especially in the multicasting service. To solve the problem, many PMIPv6-based handover schemes are proposed. However, many aspects need to improve, because there are still many redundancy signals and steps are consist in the existing schemes. In this paper, we propose a seamless handover schme to solve the weak points. An added Neighbour List Entry in MAG and a modified set of probably new LMAs can contribute to low handover latency and no packet loss. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme, we have simulated with NS-2 network simulator. The simulation result indicates that it performs a faster binding and group joining procedure.

articleTitle: The design method of the radiation source parameter-database based on C/S structure
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of unified data management for equipment EMI prediction in complex environments, this paper focuses on the key input parameters-radiation source electromagnetic characteristic parameters. In this paper, ADO.NET technology and C/S structure system are adopted to design the database system in order to integrate and classify data. Several aspects which include the development environment selection, the software framework design, the database operations and the main function of the system are taken into account to carry out the database design and implementation of radiation source electromagnetic characteristic parameters. The Electromagnetic compatibility database is developed using visual C# developing environment and SQL management system based on ADO interface technology, which improves efficiency and safety of the input parameter data management.

articleTitle: A vector parabolic equation method for propagation predictions over flat terrains
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Starting from a parabolic approximation to the Helmholtz equation, a three-dimensional (3-D) vector parabolic equation (PE) method for propagation predictions over flat terrains is presented. The split-step Fourier transform (SSFT) algorithm is adopted to solve the vector parabolic equation obtained. Besides, the impedance boundary condition is studied, as well as the absorbing boundary condition. Finally, in order to validate the proposed method, several numerical simulations of a typical flat terrain are made by using the 3-D PE method and some other methods respectively, and as a result, great agreements are observed.

articleTitle: Modeling of 1D graphene based on LTJEC-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method for modeling of graphene sheets using finite-difference time-domain method based on Laplace transform current density convolution (LTJEC-FDTD) has been proposed. The modeling of graphene sheets is achieved by obtaining recursive Maxwell's equations of tangential electric field components on graphene and current density using LTJEC. The proposed numerical formulation is compared with analytical results for validating the results.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS reduction based on polarization conversion metasurface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel type of ultra-thin polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) that reduce radar cross section (RCS) for planar structure is presented. The proposed PCM is consist of split-ring resonators. By the design with mirror-arrangement of the PCM unit cell, a strong phase cancellation is achieved. The simulation results show that the proposed PCM can realize 5 dB RCS reduction in wide range from 8.6GHz to 24.5GHz under both x- and y-polarized normal incidence, and the relative bandwidth reaches up to 96%. With respect to the published designs, the proposed metasurface has a compact profile and simple geometry but a high efficient performance, and can be widely used in radar stealth platform.

articleTitle: A compact printed MIMO antenna for UWB application with WLAN band-rejected
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact printed ultrawideband (UWB) multiple input multiple output (MIMO) is presented in this letter. The designed antenna has a size of 55 × 26 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and operates over the frequency band between 3.7-12 GHz for S11 is lower than -10dB with one notch frequency band between 5.1-12 GHz (WLAN band). Results show that the isolation is better than -17.5 dB (-22dB in 91 % of the band). The proposed antenna is suitable for practical portable MIMO/diversity UWB application.

articleTitle: Focused field estimation of time reversal waves from wireless sensors in scattered environments
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radiation safety always goes the top priority in wireless biosensor networks. As a spatial-temporal focusing transmission technique, time reversal (TR) provides an effective approach to adaptively focus the electromagnetic energy on the intended biosensor nodes so that the essential bio-tissues of the body nearby the nodes can be protected from strong electromagnetic radiation. However, the focused field intensity of TR waves around the intended biosensor nodes is typically distinguished due to different placement of nodes and different operating environments. In order to quickly estimate the focused field distribution, we develop an inverse ray (IR) model based on the principle of reversibility. This model provides a simple and fast means to characterize the intensity distribution of the focused electromagnetic fields around the biosensor nodes. The effectiveness of the analytical model has been numerically validated by the results obtained from the accurate electromagnetic field solver.

articleTitle: Denoising effect evaluation indexes for EME measurement spectrum
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Since some Gaussian noises may attach to the Electromagnetic Environment (EME) measurement spectrum, it's difficult to analyze test data or extract feature. There are some denoising methods, but we do not have any evaluation indexes to judge the effect of denoising methods. In view of this situation, a set of denoising effect evaluation indexes based on spectrum features is proposed in this paper. The indexes are including the Ratio of Gaussian Noise Square Sum (), the envelope compression ratio and the trend fitting degree. Using these indexes, we can put forward the denoising effect evaluation standard of the EME measurement spectrum. Moreover, we can use these indexes to optimize the parameters of denoising method. The effectiveness of these indexes are also showed using experiment validation in this paper.

articleTitle: Propagation of electromagnetic wave in a magnetized and non-uniform plasma
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The propagation properties of THz electromagnetic wave (EM wave) in a magnetized plasma which is inhomogeneous in both collision frequency and electron density are analyzed theoretically in this study. By utilizing the scattering matrix method (SMM) method, the effects of Electron density, collision frequency, the thickness of the plasma and the electron temperature on the absorption coefficient are analyzed numerically. It is found that these plasma parameters can cause significant change in the absorption spectra. Specifically speaking, the characteristics of the absorption coefficient, absorption peak, and absorption valley are all influenced by these typical parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis on ship's underwater static electric field with physical scale model
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the experimentation system of underwater electric field, the corrosion related static electric field produced by ship's physical scale model in the context of simulated seawater, is measured and analyzed, to investigate the distribution of ship's static electric field. Several instances are discussed, with different position arrangement or output electric current of anodes. It may provide theoretical reference for the naval ship's stealth design based on the control of electric field characteristic.

articleTitle: Multi-zone small slope approximation on dune surface scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a barchan surface is chosen as a geometrical model which has a enough high dune and could be divided into five zones where each facet has nearly similar normal vector. Then each zone has a average local normal vector which is different from others. The local incident wave vector and the local scattered wave vector of each zone are obtained by the local normal vector. The conventional small slope approximation could be applied in the local coordinate of each zone. Finally, the local scattered wave vectors of each zone are synthesized in the global coordinate. So we called the method "Multi-zone Small Slope Approximation". The results show that the cross-polarization could be obtained in the global incident plane and the reciprocity is proved by both similar cross-polarizations.

articleTitle: A novel omnidirectional circular polarized antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel omnidirectional circular polarized antenna array is proposed in this paper. The good omnidirectional circular polarization characteristic is realized by adjusting the separation distance between the dipoles and the dip angle relative to the horizontal direction. Reasonable agreement is gotten between the measured and simulated results of the reflection coefficient, AR, radiation pattern and gain of the antenna.

articleTitle: Difference field scattering properties between inlaid redundant particles and slightly rough optical surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Combing the practical situation of nondestructive examination, the analysis of difference field scattering properties between slightly rough optical surface and inlaid particles are researched by the method of Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD). In view of the half-space problem about optical surface and inlaid particles, The perfectly matched layer (PML) is used. The reciprocity theorem is applied to near-far field extrapolation. Bistatic radar cross section and difference bistatic radar cross section are analyzed between one or double redundant particles and slightly rough optical surface with different incident angles and different distances by numerical calculation. The scattering contribution and difference field scattering angular distribution of the redundant particles or slightly rough optical surface are provided.

articleTitle: A study on fluctuant target detection based on fluctuation factor
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the impact of fluctuant characteristic on target detection, a more accurate RCS fluctuant statistical model for a typical target is established and applied based on the fluctuation factor. Firstly, the dynamic RCS data were gained based on quasi-static method. Secondly, the optimal fluctuation factor was attained after fitted with Chi-square distribution based on the principle of minimal average variance. Finally, according to the relationship between target echo and RCS and combining the probability distribution it obeyed, the relationship among detection probability, SNR (Signal Noise Ratio) and fluctuation factor was researched. The result shows that an obvious direct ratio relationship exists between detection probability and fluctuation factor when the SNR is within some limit. The research of this paper is of significance to the improvement of radar's capability.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of signatures and contributing factors of atmospheric ducts based on the sounding data
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As one special type of atmospheric refraction, duct can make VHF-band radio waves and above form transhorizon propagation, playing an important role in communication and radar detection. So it is necessary to study the characteristics and contributing factors of duct. Based on the sounding data in Qingdao during 2005-2013, the signatures of duct, temperature inversion and intense humidity gradient are analyzed. The results of statistic show that temperature inversion and intense humidity gradient have a bearing on the occurrence of ducts while the effect of intense humidity gradient is more remarkable and direct compared to temperature inversion.

articleTitle: Backward scattering from the 2-D time-varying rough overturning wave crest by MoM
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Overturning wave cast is considered to be a reason of sea-spike generation, which increases the risk of radar false alarms. Therefore, study of the electromagnetic scattering of overturning wave crest is of great significance. In this paper, the improved two-dimensional (2-D) time-varying rough overturning wave crest is modeled. And the method of moment (MoM) was employed to investigate HH and VV backward scattering radar cross sections (RCS) for different incident angles, wind directions and wind speeds. Then the super phenomenon (HH polarization scattering intensity is greater than VV polarization scattering intensity) occurs frequently in the case of low grazing angle (LAG) and in some time samples as variations in the overturning wave crest. Moreover, Doppler spectra is also analyzed for the time-varying rough overturning wave crest model.

articleTitle: Design of a tunable polarization insensitive graphene absorber operating at terahertz band
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recently graphene has attracted tremendous attention for its excellent properties Numerous novel graphene-based devices have come out, showing great potential of graphene for tunable applications at THz band In this paper, by stacking a monolayer of graphene on the top of the polymer substrate, a graphene-based tunable absorber is obtained owning to the voltage-controllable conductivity of graphene. Furthermore, the absorption spectra for different chemical potentials is discussed in detail. The resonance frequency of the absorber is blue-shift with increasing chemical potential. In addition, the proposed absorber shows a good stability with various polarizations due to the symmetry of the structure. These simulated results will provide approaches to obtain dynamically switchable absorbers with a compact dimension, and such design also has potential applications in THz detection, thermal emitters, sensors and THz stealth technology.

articleTitle: A study of multi-frequency GNSS ionospheric scintillations at Guilin, China
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The features of GNSS ionospheric scintillations were studied by using multi-frequency GNSS measurements at Guilin, China (25.29°N, 110.33°E; geomagnetic: 15.04°N, 181.98°E), a station located near the northern crest of the equatorial anomaly. The results are presented for data recorded by a GPStation6 receiver from July 2015 to June 2016. The results show that amplitude scintillations were observed at night, and they mainly took place in September, October and November of 2015. However, few scintillation events occurred in 2016. The influence of ionospheric scintillations on different frequency GNSS signals is different. It is found that the new civilian signals L2C (1.2276 GHz) and L5 (1.17645 GHz) are more adversely affected than L1C/A (1.57542 GHz) signal during scintillations. And the influence of scintillations on L2C and L5 signals is similar. Ionospheric scintillations are more likely to cause L2C and L5 signals to lose phase lock. Moreover, nighttime scintillations always occurred with TEC (Total Electron Content) depletions. And the variation tendencies of TEC obtained from two different carrier phase combinations (namely, L1C/A and L2C, L1C/A and L5) are same.

articleTitle: Research on RCS time series of ballistic missile warhead in reentry phase
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the appearance of plasmasphere when ballistic missile enters in reentry phase at the speed of supersonic, impacts of reentry plasma parameter on the real RCS value of warhead are studied. According to the calculating method of dynamic RCS time series, the model is established to simulate electromagnetic scattering of reentry ballistic missile. By simplifying the trajectory reasonably, the model analyzes the change of RCS time series based on three classifications, different reentry ballistic, different angles of reentry and different speeds of reentry. The conclusions can be obtained through simulation that RCS time series is a kind of practical method which is fundamental for classification and identification of reentry ballistic missile warhead.

articleTitle: A design of dielectric lens loaded antenna array for beam steering
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to steer the beam of antenna array by loaded dielectric lens. The particular application demands the array has maximum gain and distinct beam point but the traditional methods are unallowable, such as phaser. Consequently, Dielectric lens loading is put forward to realize the demand. The effect of parameters of the dielectric lens is studied firstly. Then, the paper researches a rectangular slot antenna array with 36 units in line working in P band. The array can be achieved the gain as high as 14.3dB with the maximum point at 0 degree. A dielectric lens is designed to cover the array to steer the beam to 5 degree in demand successfully with the gain slight higher to 14.7dB for its beam width turning to be a little narrow. The simulation results illustrate the method is valuable.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering characteristics analysis of slits based on fast backprojection imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The images of a metal plate with a slit are obtained under various observation angles, by means of the method of moment and fast backprojection algorithm. Meanwhile, the impact on slit diffraction of edge diffraction and corner diffraction is eliminated through low reflection carrier design, image capture and RCS reconstruction method. Then, the slit RCS on a metal plate versus incident angles is given, and the variation of the slit RCS on a metal plate versus frequency, polarization, slit width and plate thickness are analyzed, which provides a basis for the low reflection target RCS prediction and suppression.

articleTitle: Study on the scattering property of gradient index metasurfaces with H-shaped patches
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: H-shaped patches with different sizes are used to design the gradient index surfaces for changing the phase of reflected wave along the surface, so the reflected wave from the surface can be distributed in a wide angular range, as a result, the backward radar cross section (RCS) can be reduced significantly. The whole surfaces are divided into several sections, and wave numbers in different sections are different, so that the incident wave can be reflected into different directions in the far region. The gradient index surfaces are simulated by HFSS. Comparing with the perfect electronic conducting plate (PEC) with the same size, the backward RCS of the gradient index surfaces can be reduced as large as 12 dB.

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission coefficients of moving dielectric in half space
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the coefficients of reflection and transmission of high-speed dielectric target is discussed by Lorentz-FDTD method. In this method, two coordinate systems are defined, one is the laboratory coordinate system, marked by K; another is the moving coordinate system, marked by K'. The Lorentz transformation and interpolation are used to connect the laboratory coordinate system and the moving coordinate system. The electromagnetic reflection and transmission coefficients of high-speed dielectric target are calculated. By comparing the simulation result and the analytical result, it is shown that there are a good agreement between the simulation results and the analytical results.

articleTitle: A new hybrid data compression algorithm for weather radar
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The existent problem of the weather radar data lies in its too large data which is not conducive to its storage and transmission. This paper put forward a hybrid compression algorithm of the weather radar data that consists of three steps including pre-compression, lossy compression and lossless compression. Firstly, the paper introduced the radar data's types and characteristics, analyzing the pre-compression algorithm; Secondly, according to the practical requirements of the diverse users, it proposed the adoption of lossless compression and lossy compression algorithm for the data; Finally, the flow chart of mixed compression algorithm was presented and verified based on the actual data.

articleTitle: Design of a 5-states reconfigurable filter based on the structure of SIR
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The rapid development of modern wireless communication system has greatly promoted the development of the reconfigurable filters. This paper presents a hexagonal structure reconfigurable filter which operates at five different frequencies. The resonant characteristics of stepped impedance resonator (SIR) is utilized by equaling the transmission line of low impedance to multiple parallel lines of high impedance. And four PIN diodes are loaded to control the access state of equivalent lines of high impedance. The filter operates at 2GHz, 2.3GHz, 2.5GHz, 2.7GHz and 3GHz, with 3dB absolute bandwidth of constant 100MHz. Experimental results agree well with theoretical and simulated predications.

articleTitle: An in-orbit external calibration method for antenna error of aperture synthetic radiometer
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the aperture synthetic radiometer system, the calibration of phase error plays an important role in improving the image quality. Errors of both antenna and receiving channel will cause aperture synthetic phase error in each sub-aperture, so arouse deterioration in image quality. An in-orbit external calibration method for aperture synthetic radiometer using external calibration sources on ground is proposed, mainly aiming at the calibration of the antenna pattern error and the antenna position error. The simulation shows that the method can correct these two errors well.

articleTitle: Low latitude ionospheric tomography based on the multi-station method
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As an important parameter in the process of ionospheric tomography, TEC (Total Electron Content) plays an important role in the high accuracy inversion of the ionospheric electron density. In this paper, two methods are introduced to calculate the absolute TEC including two-station method and multi-station method. Then we make a thorough performance evaluation for these two methods. After the computation of absolute TEC, the MART method is used to analyze the ionospheric electron density in the mid and low latitude regions. So we can find the variation of electron density with latitude and the differences between day and night from the measure data.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a novel C broadband phased-array antenna element
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the requirement of phased-array antenna, a novel C broadband phased-array antenna element is designed and implemented. A new structure is applied: 4 cell antennas are combined through two-stage passive combiner, between which a band pass filter is added to restrain the out-of-band signals. Simulation and test data shows that the SWR is less than 1.5 within 22% of the band width, gain of the antenna element is more than 10dB, and the side-lobe is 12dB lower than the main lobe in directivity diagram of the E-plane. It is suitable for application of C broadband phased-array antennas.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily non-conformal ellipsoidal invisible cloak
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: According to the linear coordinate transformation of metamaterial, we design 3-D arbitrarily non-conformal ellipsoidal cloaks, that is the inner and outer ellipsoidal shell has different focus, while existing theories about ellipsoidal cloak are confocal. Theoretical derivation about the permittivity and permeability tensors of metamaterial is demonstrated in this letter. We notice those tensors are inhomogeneous and anisotropic. Full wave simulation are implemented to verify the arbitrarily non-conformal ellipsoidal cloaks.

articleTitle: RCS reduction of active periodical structural scatterer
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A model of novel periodical structural scatterer is proposed in this paper. After the operation of wire connection, the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of the diamond patch array has been decreased dramatically from the simulation and experimental results. When the impedance controllable network composed of varactor diodes is loaded between the unit cells, the RCS of scatterer could be tuned by different biasing voltage at L-band frequencies. The experimental results demonstrate the validity of this technology that the RCS of the active scatterer can be reduced more than 10 dB in a wide angle range.

articleTitle: Artificial negative refraction index material consisting of dielectric perpendicular rings
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We present a detailed study on the artificial negative index refraction behavior of the composite metamaterial consisting of high-permittivity dielectric rings. The rings array in cubic lattice arrangement can exhibit an negative magnetism when excited into magnetic dipole resonance. Full-wave simulations show that the bulk metamaterial with this structure can exhibit a negative refraction behavior. It is shown that artificial magnetic response can originate from differently structured dielectric elements, similarly to the conventional metamaterial constituents based on metal resonance structures.

articleTitle: Investigatiaon on the far-field characteristic of radar radiant source in ship fleet
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Reliable and accurate propagation path loss prediction between radar radiant sources and susceptive equipments necessitates a good understanding of electromagnetic wave scattering in the presence of inhomogeneous atmosphere near sea, and this is one of the major issues in ship fleet electromagnetic compatibility literature. For sake of this reason to solving the far field of the radar radiant source inner the ship fleets, this paper proposed a wide-ranging applicability method to compute the far field of the radar on the Shipboard. These methods take some factors into attention, such as the reflectivity of the rough sea surface, the multipath loss, and globe curvature, and can compute the magnitude of the far field of the radar mounted on shipboard. The computed model of the far field of the radar in ship fleet can provide electromagnetic environments parameters, further, can be used into the electromagnetic compatibility analysis of the whole ship fleet. Then the computed model of the far field of the radar in ship fleet is certificated by the measurements, and is used to investigate the far field characteristic of radar radiant source in ship fleet.

articleTitle: Nondata-aided timing recovery for partial response CPM
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Timing recovery for the binary partial response continuous phase modulation (CPM) is investigated in this paper and a feedforward nondata-aided (NDA) timing algorithm suitable for CPM signals with different modulation indices is proposed. In the algorithm several autocorrelation functions are computed based on the sampled received signal and the lag in the autocorrelation functions is carefully selected depending on the modulation index. And then the timing offset is estimated based on the autocorrelations. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm works well when the modulation index is at a range of 1/3 to 2/3 and has better performance at higher modulation indices. Additionally, the mean square error of the proposed algorithm can be decreased considerably compared with the existing feedforward NDA timing algorithm.

articleTitle: Dumbbell slots coulping circular polarization high gain antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A circularly polarized microstrip antenna with high gain was proposed in this paper. The radiator is on the bottom of the upper substrate. The ground with two orthogonal dumbbell is on the top of the lower substrate. In order to improve antenna gain significantly, a reflector is used. It is air between the upper substrate and the lower substrate. The dumbbell shape slots are fed by a power divider with phase difference of 90 degrees. The simulated impedance bandwidth, the axial ratio bandwidth of the antenna are 2.21-2.55GHz and 2.22-2.38GHz, respectively and circular polarization gain is more than 8.2dB, which are basically consistent with the measured results.

articleTitle: A new brightness temperature model for low elevation angles and application in remote sensing of evaporation ducts
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: At present, ground-based microwave radiometers are widely used for remote sensing of atmosphere, observing at elevation angles more than 15° with an atmospheric profile retrieval model, no considering the effects of atmospheric refraction and sea surface emission. In this paper, a low elevation angle brightness temperature model is proposed, taking the effects of atmospheric refraction, sea surface reflection and emission into account. The differences between the two models are simulated and compared, of which the reasons and mechanisms are analyzed. Results show that, at elevation angles less than 5 effects of atmospheric refraction or sea surface emission could not be cancelled. Lastly, applications of low elevation angle brightness temperature model in remote sensing of evaporation ducts are simulated, from which one can find that brightness temperatures at low elevation angles are sensitive to evaporation ducts and lower tropospheric profiles.

articleTitle: Automatic detection of ionospheric TEC depletions by using low-latitude GNSS data
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a method has been developed to automatically detect and characterize low-latitude ionospheric plasma bubbles which are a main source of scintillation effects. When the ionosphere is monitored by using GNSS beacon, plasma bubbles appear as TEC (total electron content) depletions. Therefore, plasma bubbles can be detected by identifying TEC depletions. This method of automatic detection is based on the variations of the slope of the relative TEC and the variance of the slope. The general characteristics of ionospheric TEC depletions, such as geographical location, beginning-time, ending-time and depth, can be provided automatically by this method. The reliability of this method is tested by using GNSS measurements recorded at Guilin during March 2014. The results show a good consistency between the automatic and manual identification.

articleTitle: Seasonal occurrence of polar mesosphere summer echo variations with different layers
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Polar Mesosphere Summer Echoes (PMSE) are strong radar echoes that have been observed typically by the VHF radar in summer polar mesosphere and have closely relation with charged dust particles. Theoretical analysis and extensive experimental data show that polar mesosphere summer echoes (PMSE) present some kind of regular periodic changes, such as semidiurnal variations, diurnal variations, day-to-day variations, seasonal variations, year-to-year variations, obvious layered phenomena and so on. To obtain the trends of PMSE occurrence rate with different layers, data detected by the European Incoherent Scatter Scientific Association (EISCAT) VHF radar in 12 years is used to analyze corresponding PMSE occurrence. The year-to-year variations of PMSE occurrence rate with one-, two- and triple-layered are given, and the effect of geomagnetic activities are discussed in the paper. The results indicate new recommendation for studying PMSE in the future.

articleTitle: On the directivities of harmonic and spurious emission of phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The generation mechanism of harmonic and spurious emission in the phased array radar transmitting channels are analyzed. The channels components' influence on the phase of the harmonic and spurious emission are presented. The phase of harmonic and spurious emission at the stimulating ports of antenna elements are presented as well. The beam direction of harmonic and spurious emission in line array and plan array are analyzed. The array factors of the harmonic and spurious emission are simulated, which proves the emission of harmonic has directivity and the emission of spurious emission are randomly distributed. The experiments validating the analysis are performed.

articleTitle: Study and design of ultra-broadband loaded monopole antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a ultra-broadband loaded monopole antenna. To broaden the operation bandwidth of the monopole antenna and efficiently resolve the problem of the nulls of the antenna pattern, a novel antenna design method is proposed by loading with lumped elements. The loads are parallel resistor/inductor (RL) circuits. The loaded antenna having a larger bandwidth, with the maximum gain is almost at the horizontal radiation direction. Finally the gain of the system is greater than -5 dBi over the entire frequency band of operation.

articleTitle: Time and spectrum domain analysis of electromagnetic pulse
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic pulse is a threaten to electron equipment. This paper analyzies the feature of pulse in time and frequency domain, researches the impact of pulse parameter, such as risingtime, fallingtime, pulse width, and the conclusion is obtained. To obtain the feature of spectrum distribution, this paper carries out spectrum cutting analysis. The results of analysis can be a reference to pulse protect design.

articleTitle: One case about comparison of PMSE heating effect with two different radar echoes layers
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: From EISCAT VHF radar observations it is evident that polar mesosphere summer echoes (PMSE) often show obvious layers. PMSE overshoot describe the effect of dusty plasma parameters on overshoot characteristics curve. In this paper we obtain and compare different PMSE overshoot characteristic curves (OCCs) at 80-85 km and 85-90 km in one hour respectively, from based on the data observed by EISCAT 224 MHz VHF radar on 12 July 2007. The relate intensity of PMSE on the moment when the heater off show some different characteristics in different PMSE layers.

articleTitle: A wideband and high-gain magneto-electric dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel wideband high-gain Magneto-Electric dipole antenna is presented. The proposed Magneto-Electric antenna is composed of a fishtail-shaped electric dipole, a half-circular loop antenna that works as a magnetic dipole, a microstrip-to-coplanar stripline transition balun, a box-shaped reflector and the loading of T-shaped array of metamaterial elements on the dielectric substrate. A high gain can be realized by loading of T-shaped array of metamaterial elements and using a rectangular box-shaped reflector. Simulated results show that this antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 58.5%, ranging from 2.32 GHz to 4.24 GHz and a high gain about 8 dB. Moreover, radiation patterns with low back radiation, fixing broadside direction mainbeam, symmetrical E- and H-plane patterns and large front-to-back ratio are obtained over the whole operating band by using a rectangular box-shaped reflector. The good performances make the antenna suitable for the wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Microwave technology for brain activities detection of rats
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new detection approach based on microwave transmission approach for brain neuronal activities detection is presented in this paper. The existing research shows that the dielectric at brain excited site has a dynamic nature, which gives a hope for brain neuronal activities detection by using microwave approach. Here, we discuss the principles of microwave detecting method for brain neuronal activities. A simplified model was applied in simulation to study the electromagnetic energy distribution and poynting vector. To proof the approach, we have performed an intensive study of the phase change when an EM wave propagating through the function site such that the permittivity varies. The results demonstrates that microwave can be used to detect brain activities.

Author Keywords: electromagnetic field distribution in rat head

articleTitle: Analysis and study on the prediction model of rain attenuation in short path
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It is found that the path adjustment factor or the rainfall adjustment factor achieved from most of model is greater than 1 in short path by analyzing the prediction model of rain attenuation currently available in terrestrial links. It is inconsistent with the assumption that the shorter the propagation path length is, the more uniformly distributed spatially and temporally the rainfall rate is. The measured path adjustment factor for short path is analyzed based on the ITU-R SG3 database and data measured by Chinese researchers. It can be inferred that the phenomena that the path adjustment factor or the rainfall adjustment factor obtained from the model is greater than 1 in the short distance is caused by the insufficient of ITU-R SG3 database in short path. Therefore more experimental data should be collected to make the model agree better with the experimental data in short path.

articleTitle: Channel pre-distortion compensation techniques in SAR echo simulator
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: SAR echo simulator plays an important role in space-borne SAR development. As it uses a wide signal bandwidth, the LFM signal is affected in the transmit and receive channel because of the non-linear characteristics. This paper focuses on the LFM signal channel pre-distortion compensation in the SAR echo simulator, and the concrete implementation steps in time-domain compensation are given. This proposed technique is of reliable performance and is used in the actual spaceborne SAR echo simulator.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from rough sea surface covered with oil films
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A composite random rough surface model is presented for describing rough sea surface covered with oil films, the electromagnetic wave scattering from this sea surface is studied based on the Stratton-Chu integral equations mainly. A general expression for the radar cross section is derived taking into account a modulation of the rough surface by long surface waves, and the formulae of scattering coefficient is obtained further. The curves of the scattering coefficient of HH polarization with varying of the scattering angle are obtained by numerical implementation, the influence of the root mean square and correlation function of small scale roughness, the ratio of the root mean square and correlation function of large scale roughness, wave number of space, the amplitude of spatial fluctuation, the electromagnetic wave irradiation area, the root mean square and correlation function of large scale roughness and the frequency of the incident wave on the scattering coefficient is discussed. The numerical results show that the influence of these factors on the scattering coefficient is very complex.

articleTitle: The range alignment algorithm for high-resolution range profile of multiple target
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the difficulty in the range alignment of HRRP because of more than one target in the window of radar image, this paper propose a alignment method for multiple targets in the target group by using an image segmentation method. First, we accumulate the HRRP of the target, and get the HRRP process diagram. By calculating the correlation coefficient between each frame of HRRP and the reference HRRP, the unaligned HRRP sequence is aligned roughly in frequency domain. After rough alignment, the image segmentation method is used to segment the range image of each target. In the end, the envelope alignment for the HRRP of each target is finished using the least entropy method. The algorithm is simple and fast, and can achieve a better alignment effect on multi object tracking. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the analysis of the simulation data.

articleTitle: A powerful analytic-numerical algorithm for scattering from a 3-D object above a 2-D conductive rough surface
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A multi-hybrid method combining numerical vector finite-element method/boundary integral method (FEM/BIM) and analytic Kirchhoff approximation (KA) is employed in this paper to study the scattering from a 3-D object above a 2-D conductive rough surface. The scattering from the target is studied by hybrid vector FEM/BIM while KA is applied on the underlying rough surface to reduce the computation time and memory requirement. An iterative approach is employed to take into account the multiple interaction between the target and underlying rough surface. Using the Monte Carlo method to generate 2-D Gaussian rough surface, bistatic difference field radar cross section (d-RCS) of A 3-D dielectric target above a 2D conductive rough surface is numerically simulated.

articleTitle: Implementation of a second-order ABC in TDFEM for 2D electromagnetic problems
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This letter describes a novel Time-Domain Finite-Element Method based second-order Engquist-Majda ABC. In order to improve the accuracy, a specific corner condition is introduced at the corners of the external boundary. For the discretization of time derivatives, the Newmark method is used to obtain an unconditionally stable scheme with the second-order accuracy. Numerical results are presented showing the validity of the presented method.

articleTitle: Low profile and wideband circular polarized microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a low profile and wideband antenna array with circular polarization. The antenna consists of 2 × 2 elements. Loop coupled structure and sequential rotation feeding technique are used to obtained wideband VSWR and axial ratio performances. The proposed antenna array is analyzed with HFSS software. The VSWR, Axial Ratio, and Radiation Patterns of the array are presented. The simulated results show that the VSWRs are below 1.5 over the frequency band of 1.88–2.26 GHz while the axial ratio is below 3.0 dB over the band of 1.96–2.25 GHz

articleTitle: A dynamic electromagnetic scattering simulation method based on polarization transform
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming to the dynamic electromagnetic characteristic of the space target, a high-effective and real-time simulation method is proposed to suffice the demand of the engineering project. Firstly, use the coordinate transform means to calculate the pitch and aspect angle of Line of Sight(LOS) in the radar reference frame; And, calculate the rotate angle between the polarization basis vector of the target reference frame and the radar reference frame; Finally, the dynamic full-polar electromagnetic characteristic is acquired by the polar transform matrix. The examination analyzes the dynamic scattering characteristic of the typical space target in flying process. The proposed method is consistent with the common interpolation method based on static full polarization data, which indicates that the dynamic characteristic of target is related to the polarization basis of the radar sensor. And the validity of the method is proved.

articleTitle: Diagnose the marine atmospheric duct using satellite remote sensing technique
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric duct can exert an important influence on radio wave propagation in the lower atmosphere, especially over oceanic or coastal locations. The refractivity profiles in duct are the requirement for input to the radio wave propagation model and predict the effects of radars. Considering the satellite sensing technique development, we pose a method to fuse the Satellite Electromagnetic Electro-Optical (SEMO) technique and evaporation model for the atmospheric duct diagnose and refractivity profiles determination.

articleTitle: Tuning technique of the loaded active radar absorber
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a tunable active frequency selective surface (AFSS) absorber with different loaded methods is designed. The top layer is a substrate which holds up the AFSS. The second layer is an AFSS, which is composed of a frequency selective surface (FSS) and some PIN diodes. The third layer is an insulator composed of foam material. Reflectance measurement shows that the reflection characteristic of the AFSS absorber could be effectively controlled by adjusting the dc voltage of the PIN diode. In addition, the reflectivity could be dynamically adjusted by sine wave. When the frequency of the sine wave was 100 KHz, 1 MHz or 5 MHz, the reflectivity of AFSS could be less than -10 dB at the frequency band of 3.2~5.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of computerized ionospheric tomography using PALSAR polarimetric data
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The computerized ionospheric tomography (CIT) technique is a means to obtain the spatial distribution of ionospheric electron density from the TEC values, which can be realized by the ground-based GPS. In this paper, by using the ALOS Phased Array L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR) full-pol data and ionospheric data from the IRI 2007, the reconstruction of ionospheric electron density distribution is first proposed. Simulation results show that it can demonstrate the spatial distribution of ionospheric electron density. Compared with GPS measurements, the proposed technique do not needs ground stations and can give a higher resolution results due to the characters of space-borne SAR systems. Thus, it is a promising direction in future CIT.

articleTitle: A robust timing recovery algorithm with frequency offset for MIL-STD SOQPSK
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A robust timing recovery algorithm for military standard (MIL-STD) shaped-offset quadrature phase-shift keying (SOQPSK) is presented and this scheme can be used in the signal with frequency offset. The new algorithm is based on the correlation calculation, and the timing offset information is extracted by the absolution operation to the correlation function. The theoretical analysis and the simulation result both show that the provided scheme can work well to the MIL-STD SOQPSK signal with frequency offset.

articleTitle: An analytical solution to the scattering by gyrotropic anisotropic spherical shell
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic fields in gyrotropic anisotropic spherical shell can be expressed as the addition of the first and second spherical vector wave functions in gyrotropic anisotropic medium. Applying the boundary conditions of electromagnetic fields in the interface of gyrotropic anisotropic spherical shell's medium, the expansion coefficients of electromagnetic fields in terms of spherical vector wave functions in gyrotropic anisotropic medium and free space can be derived, and then the radar cross sections (RCSs) of a plane wave scattering by gyrotropic anisotropic spherical shell can be obtained. Numerical results for the very general gyrotropic dielectric medium are obtained and those in special cases are compared between the present method and homogeneous gyrotropic anisotropic sphere or plasma spherical shell, they are agreement very well.

articleTitle: An improved hybrid FEM/MOM combining MLFMA for composite electromagnetic scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A generalized hybrid scheme combining finite element method (FEM) and the method of moments (MoM) accelerated by multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is first presented to investigate scattering from a 3-D dielectric object above a 2-D electrically large dielectric rough surface. The hybrid FEM/ MoM scheme is divided into the FEM region for the object based on Helmholtz's equation and the MOM region for the rough surface based on coupled integral function, which can greatly reduce the computed region. MLFMA is employed to reduce computation complexity of MOM region itself and coupling interaction matrices between MOM region and FEM region. Consequently the iterative solving process can be greatly accelerated. This genralized hybrid FEM/MOM is very suitable for investigating scattering characteristics of composite model composed of a complex material object and electrically large dielectric rough surface. Some examples verify this generalized hybrid FEM/MOM features high efficiency, low storage requirement, high accuracy and generality.

articleTitle: The analysis on Doppler spectrum of 2-D sea clutter in multi-band
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Multi-band Doppler spectrum of radar clutter at there-dimensional sea surface is calculated in this paper, the Elfouhaily sea spectrum with a direction function is applied to achieving the scattering fields is a classic PO method. Analysis on the spectrum width and shift of multi-band can be done. Larger spectrum width and shift have been seen in larger wind speed in high frequency. By applying the Doppler model to the data, it is possible to extract the Bragg scattering polarization ratio, and the two non-Bragg scattering mechanisms can also be studied, this is what the process in this paper means.

articleTitle: Research on the method of combining period extraction with eigenvalue entropy
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The echo of target with micro-motion contains the electromagnetic scattering characteristics and movement characteristics, which plays important roles in the target identification. Precession period is one of the important characteristics on the analysis of the micro-motion characteristics. Aimed at the phenomenon of extracting the cycle of no precession target, in the thesis a method is proposed by combing period extraction with eigenvalue entropy. The original echo is constructed by establishing autocorrelation matrix and the eigenvalues are obtained through eigenvalue decomposition. Then the period is extracted after calculating the eigenvalue entropy. The method can eliminate some targets with no obvious precession and minish the error of period extraction.

articleTitle: A novel design approach for wideband absorber screen
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel design approach to the absorber screen based on the receiving antenna technique is presented in this letter. According to the similar performance principle of absorber and receiving antenna, the dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna is improved and optimized by the software HFSS to obtain a thin and broadband absorber screen. And the simulation result shows that a 78% wide band for -10dB power reflection reduction is achieved. Meanwhile, the thickness of absorber screen is below 1/9 of the wavelength at the center frequency in free space.

articleTitle: The optimal order of processing sensors in sequential IPDA filter
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The sequential integrated Probabilistic Data Association (IPDA) is derived in the RFS framework. It is shown that the sequential IPDA filter depends on the order in which the sensors are used. Generally, it is difficult to obtain the optimal order of processing sensor in the sequential IPDA filter for general cases. In this paper, several rules for obtaining the optimal order are discussed using the normalization factor of the Bayesian recursion.

articleTitle: A TE01 generator excited by TEM
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An efficient TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-mode generator excited by coaxial-waveguide TEM mode is proposed with high mode purity. Simulations show the generator operating at 35GHz can give a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> conversion efficiency of 97.5% and mode purity of 99.8% which higher than the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> generator available at present.

articleTitle: Design of overmoded-waveguide directional coupler and correction of coupling coefficient calculation
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of high-power microwave system, a novel overmoded-waveguide directional coupler centred at 2.4 GHz, with low coupling of 40-50 dB, and with directivity greater than 20dB, is designed. A resonant cavity as the transition waveguide between main waveguide and sub-waveguide is introduced. This paper also proposes a correction of coupling coefficient calculation. Ultimately, after optimizing the parameters, a structure with good performance is obtained.

articleTitle: A robust interference alignment algorithm and the system design
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an interference alignment algorithm named Robust Weighted Minimum Mean Square Error(R-WMMSE) algorithm. We also design a 3-user wireless communication system which considers realization factors to evaluate the performance of the R-WMMSE algorithm. The system is realized through a system level simulation, both in floated-point and fixed-point manner. The results suggest that the algorithm work well in real communication systems. The impact of Line-of-Sight in Rician channel is also investigated.

articleTitle: Design of ultra-wideband bow-tie antenna in UHF band
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband bow-tie antenna that works at ultrahigh frequency (UHF) by utilizing microstrip balun and loading with the cavity-backed is presented. By connecting two folded elements to the patches of the bowtie dipole, the compact dimensions of the antenna can be achieved. The proposed antenna has an operating bandwidth ranging from f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> to f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (relative bandwidth above 108.5%), which fulfills the requirement of UWB antenna. The measurement results show that the VSWR is less than 2 in the operating bandwidth. The proposed antenna also provides stable peak gain, unidirectional radiation patterns, a small volume and an ultra-wideband.

articleTitle: Power frequency electromagnetic interference test and analysis of the rail weighbridge pressure sensor
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: From the field test found that the data of rail weighbridge pressure appear sine wave whose frequency is 50Hz. In order to solve this engineering problem, we studied the electromagnetic compatibility of rail weighbridge pressure sensor. First of all, we analyzed the principle of pressure sensor. Then, we tested the field strength of signal lines and power cord, testing the voltage between cable shielded layer and the earth. Through the theoretical analysis and calculation of field intensity around the signal cable, we found that cable shielded layer as interference sources cause interference to the signal conductor. Circuit model analysis of shielding layer caused by parasitic capacitance coupling between the core mechanism of deformation compression case study analyzes the shielded cable for signal transmission. Through theory and simulation analysis, it is concluded that the shield potential changes, conductor and shield interference between the change of the coupling capacitance of conductor.

articleTitle: Generating broadband Cherenkov radiation with low energy electrons based on plasmonic graded grating
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Generating Cherenkov-radiation (CR) with plasmonic graded metallic grating is proposed and studied. The simulation shows CR could be obtained even with electron energy as low as 2.5keV and the frequency range covers 0.15 to 0.5THz.

articleTitle: Density and temperature characteristics of hypersonic aircraft outflow field near the wall
publicationTitle: 2016 11th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: When flying at a high speed or ultra-high speed, The hypersonic aircraft will react violently with the flow nearby. So some density and temperature distribution characteristics appear near the wall. These features will affect the optical imaging system resolution of the target image, and generate pneumatic optical effect. In this paper, we established two optical-hood models of aircraft with different half cone angles by using CFD simulation technology. Fluent were then used to simulate the temperature and density distribution of flow field near the models with different Mach numbers on the same flight altitude. Finally, we studied the variation characteristic of temperature and density with distance increasing from the wall. These studies have reference value on the design of ultra high-speed aircraft and aero-optical bias correction. Besides, improving the optical imaging system in the target image sharpness.
